short_description.id: Water bull (tarbh-uisge) adalah makhluk mitologi Skotlandia penghuni danau di padang belantara, umumnya lebih ramah daripada kuda air tetapi juga amfibi dan dapat berubah wujud.
short_description.en: The water bull (tarbh-uisge) is a Scottish mythological creature of moorland lochs, usually friendlier than the water horse but likewise amphibious and shapeshifting.

long_description.id: Water bull, juga disebut tarbh-uisge dalam bahasa Gaelik Skotlandia (Scottish Gaelic), adalah makhluk mitologi Skotlandia (Scottish) yang mirip tarroo ushtey dari Manx dan tarbh-uisce dari Irlandia (Irish). Umumnya dianggap penghuni malam danau (loch) di padang belantara, ia biasanya lebih ramah daripada padanannya, kuda air, tetapi memiliki kemampuan amfibi dan berubah wujud yang serupa. Ia dikatakan kawin dengan sapi biasa, dan keturunannya dapat dikenali dari telinganya yang kecil; menurut sebagian mitos, anak sapi itu harus dibunuh saat lahir dengan cara apa pun selain ditenggelamkan.
long_description.en: The water bull, called tarbh-uisge in Scottish Gaelic, is a Scottish mythological creature akin to the Manx tarroo ushtey and the Irish tarbh-uisce. Usually seen as a night-dwelling resident of moorland lochs, it is generally kinder than its horse counterpart, the water horse, though it has the same amphibious and shape-changing powers. It is said to breed with ordinary cattle, its calves known by their small ears; in some myths such calves must be killed at birth by any means except drowning.

long_description.id: Leksikografer Edward Dwelly menerjemahkan tarbh-uisge sebagai "banteng air, banteng laut atau sapi" (ajaib); tarbh berarti banteng dan uisge berarti air. Kepercayaan akan water bull bertahan di Skotlandia setidaknya hingga akhir abad ke-19. Ia dapat berubah menjadi manusia dan hidup di darat maupun air; ia bisa menjadi binatang hitam jahat yang mengerikan, tetapi tidak sejahat each-uisge, dan bisa pula ramah dan menolong. Menurut artikel fr, di wilayah utara anak sapi keturunannya justru dianggap berkualitas unggul.
long_description.en: The lexicographer Edward Dwelly renders tarbh-uisge as 'water bull, sea bull or cow' (fabulous); tarbh means bull and uisge water. Belief in water bulls lasted in Scotland until at least the late 19th century. It can take human form and live on land or in water; it may be a monstrous, wicked black beast, though less nasty than the each-uisge, or friendly and helpful. According to the fr article, in northern areas its half-bred calves are on the contrary prized as superior.

Bhootas are said to cast no shadows and speak nasally. Crooke’s collection describes Bhut as the spirit of someone dying violently through accident, suicide, or capital punishment.

short_description.en: The karkadann is a mythical creature believed to inhabit the grassy plains of India and Iran.

long_description.id: Karkadann adalah makhluk mitos yang dipercaya hidup di padang rumput India dan Iran. Kargadan juga berarti badak dalam bahasa Persia dan Arab.
long_description.en: The karkadann is a mythical creature believed to inhabit the grassy plains of India and Iran. Kargadan also means rhinoceros in Persian and Arabic.

long_description.id: Seperti unicorn, karkadann dipercaya dapat dijinakkan oleh perawan. Gambaran karkadann awalnya didasarkan pada badak India. Al-Biruni memberikan salah satu uraian awal karkadann pada abad kesepuluh hingga kesebelas. Tanduk karkadann dipercaya memiliki daya penyembuhan.
long_description.en: Like the unicorn, the karkadann is believed to be subdued by virgins. The karkadann’s depiction is initially based on the Indian rhinoceros. Al-Biruni provides an early description of the karkadann in the tenth to eleventh century. The karkadann’s horn is believed to have healing powers.

short_description.id: Grand'Goule, "Mulut Besar", adalah naga legenda Poitiers yang memangsa biarawati di ruang bawah tanah Biara Sainte-Croix sampai diusir Santa Radegonda.
short_description.en: The Grand'Goule, 'Big Mouth', is a legendary dragon of Poitiers that devoured nuns in the cellars of the Abbey of Sainte-Croix until St Radegund drove it out.

long_description.id: Grand'Goule, "Mulut Besar" dalam dialek Poitevin, adalah naga cerita rakyat Poitiers, semacam versi lokal tarasque. Pada masa Santa Radegonda (abad ke-6) ia tinggal di dasar sungai Clain, masuk ke ruang bawah tanah saat air naik, dan memangsa biarawati Biara Sainte-Croix. Radegonda mengusirnya dengan salib kecil, air suci, dan doa, atau menurut versi lain dengan serpihan Salib Sejati, ke sungai.
long_description.en: The Grand'Goule, 'Big Mouth' in Poitevin, is a folk dragon of Poitiers, a sort of local tarasque. In St Radegund's time (6th century) it lived at the bottom of the Clain, entered the cellars when the water rose, and devoured the nuns of the Abbey of Sainte-Croix. Radegund drove it off with a small cross, holy water and prayer, or in another version with the piece of the True Cross, into the river.

long_description.id: Sebuah piagam tahun 1466 mencatat naga dalam prosesi Hari Rogasi di Poitiers. Patung kayu karya Jean Gargot (1677) diarak dalam prosesi itu sementara anak-anak melemparkan kue casse-museau dan berseru "Boune sainte veurmine"; prosesi ini berhenti pada abad ke-19 dan patungnya kini di Musée Sainte-Croix.
long_description.en: A charter of 1466 records a dragon in the Rogation procession at Poitiers. Jean Gargot's wooden statue (1677) was paraded while children threw casse-museau cakes and cried 'Boune sainte veurmine'; the procession ended in the 19th century and the statue is now in the Musée Sainte-Croix.

short_description.id: Enbarr (Aonbharr) adalah kuda dalam Siklus Mitologi Irlandia milik dewa laut Manannán mac Lir, yang dapat melintasi darat dan laut lebih cepat dari angin.
short_description.en: Enbarr (Aonbharr) is a horse of the Irish Mythological Cycle owned by the sea god Manannán mac Lir, able to cross land and sea faster than the wind.

long_description.id: Enbarr (Énbarr) atau Aonbharr milik Manannán (Irlandia/Irish: Aonbharr Mhanannáin) adalah kuda dalam Siklus Mitologi Irlandia yang dapat melintasi darat dan laut lebih cepat dari angin. Kuda itu milik dewa laut Manannan mac Lir, tetapi diserahkan kepada Lugh Lamh-fada untuk dipakainya. Dalam kisah Oidheadh Chloinne Tuireann, Lugh menolak meminjamkannya kepada putra-putra Tuireann, tetapi kemudian terpaksa meminjamkan perahu yang berlayar sendiri, Sguaba Tuinne ("Penyapu Ombak").
long_description.en: In the Irish Mythological Cycle, Enbarr (Énbarr), also Aonbharr of Manannán (Irish Aonbharr Mhanannáin), is a steed that outruns the wind over land and sea alike. It belonged to the sea god Manannan mac Lir but was given to Lugh Lamh-fada for his use. In the tale Oidheadh Chloinne Tuireann, Lugh refuses to lend it to the sons of Tuireann but is then forced to lend them the self-steering boat Sguaba Tuinne ('Wave-sweeper').

long_description.id: Makna namanya beragam: Cormac's glossary mengartikan enbarr sebagai "buih", O'Curry sebagai "Satu Surai", dan kamus James Mackillop sebagai "supremasi unik". Dalam roman itu, kuda tersebut lebih cepat dari "angin dingin musim semi", dapat melintasi darat atau laut dengan sama mudahnya, dan siapa pun yang menungganginya tak dapat dibunuh. Menurut artikel id, nama Embarr tampaknya juga dianggap kuda Niamh yang membawa Oisín dan Niamh menyeberangi laut ke Tír na nÓg, menurut karya Mícheál Coimín.
long_description.en: The meaning of the name varies: Cormac's glossary gives enbarr as 'froth', O'Curry 'One Mane', and James Mackillop's dictionary 'unique supremacy'. In the romance the horse is swifter than the 'naked cold wind of spring', goes over land or sea with equal ease, and whoever rides it cannot be killed. According to the id article the name Embarr also seems to have been taken for Niamh's horse, which carried Oisín and Niamh across the sea to Tír na nÓg in the work of Mícheál Coimín.

short_description.id: Beast of Dean adalah hewan cerita rakyat Inggris yang konon hidup di Forest of Dean, Gloucestershire, dan diburu pada awal abad ke-19 sebagai babi hutan raksasa.
short_description.en: The Beast of Dean is an animal of English folklore said to live in the Forest of Dean, Gloucestershire, hunted in the early 19th century as a giant boar.

long_description.id: Beast of Dean adalah nama hewan dari cerita rakyat Inggris (English folklore) yang konon hidup, atau pernah hidup, di Forest of Dean, hutan kuno yang luas yang dibatasi Sungai Severn dan Wye di Gloucestershire, Inggris (England). Meski ada beberapa upaya menemui, menangkap, atau membunuhnya pada awal abad ke-19, tidak ada bukti ilmiah keberadaannya. Kisah-kisahnya tampaknya berasal dari abad ke-18 atau awal abad ke-19.
long_description.en: The Beast of Dean is an animal of English folklore said to live, or once to have lived, in the Forest of Dean, a large ancient woodland between the rivers Severn and Wye in Gloucestershire, England. Despite several early 19th-century attempts to find, capture or kill it, no scientific evidence of it has been found. The tales seem to date from the 18th or early 19th century.

long_description.id: Pada 1802 para petani desa Parkend melakukan ekspedisi untuk menangkap dan membunuhnya, tetapi tidak menemukan apa pun; hewan yang mereka buru dilaporkan babi hutan yang cukup besar untuk merobohkan pohon dan pagar tanaman. Babi hutan memang masih dapat ditemukan di Forest of Dean hingga kini, tetapi banyak rujukan abad ke-20 dan ke-21 berasal dari para kriptozoolog. Pada 2007 serial televisi Primeval menampilkannya kembali sebagai gorgonopsid. Menurut artikel bg, ia juga dikenal sebagai "moose-pig".
long_description.en: In 1802 farmers from the village of Parkend set out to catch and kill it but found nothing; the animal they sought was said to be a boar big enough to fell trees and hedges. Wild boar still live in the Forest of Dean, but many 20th- and 21st-century references come from cryptozoologists. In 2007 the TV series Primeval reimagined it as a gorgonopsid. According to the bg article it is also known as the 'moose-pig'.

short_description.id: Morag adalah julukan monster danau yang diyakini banyak orang hidup di Loch Morar, Skotlandia, dan termasuk monster legenda Skotlandia yang paling banyak ditulis setelah Nessie.
short_description.en: Morag is the nickname of a loch monster many believe lives in Loch Morar, Scotland, among the most written-about Scottish monsters after Nessie.

long_description.id: Morag (Gaelik Skotlandia/Scottish Gaelic: Mòrag) adalah julukan monster danau yang diyakini banyak orang hidup di Loch Morar, Skotlandia (Scotland). Setelah Nessie, ia termasuk monster legenda Skotlandia yang paling banyak ditulis. "Morag", nama perempuan Skotlandia, adalah permainan kata atas nama danau itu. Laporan penampakan berawal sejak 1887 dan mencapai 34 kejadian pada 1981, enam belas di antaranya dengan banyak saksi.
long_description.en: Morag (Scottish Gaelic Mòrag) is the nickname of a loch monster that many people believe lives in Loch Morar, Scotland. Only Nessie has drawn more pages among Scotland's monsters of legend. 'Morag', a Scottish girl's name, puns on the loch's name. Reports go back to 1887 and had reached 34 incidents by 1981, sixteen with several witnesses.

long_description.id: Klaim yang banyak diberitakan dari Agustus 1969 melibatkan dua lelaki setempat, Duncan McDonell dan William Simpson, yang mengaku perahunya tak sengaja menabrak makhluk itu sehingga ia menyerang; McDonell menangkis dengan dayung dan Simpson menembaknya dengan senapan, lalu makhluk itu tenggelam perlahan. Mereka menggambarkannya berwarna cokelat, panjang 7,6–9,1 m, berkulit kasar, dengan tiga punuk di punggung. Menurut artikel de, Mhorag ("roh danau" dalam bahasa Gaelik) digambarkan mirip plesiosaurus dan sangat mirip monster Loch Ness.
long_description.en: A widely reported claim of August 1969 involved two local men, Duncan McDonell and William Simpson, who said their boat accidentally struck the creature and it attacked; McDonell fended it off with an oar and Simpson fired his rifle, after which it slowly sank. They described it as brown, 7.6–9.1 m long, rough-skinned, with three humps on its back. According to the de article Mhorag ('spirit of the loch' in Gaelic) is described as plesiosaur-like and very similar to the Loch Ness Monster.

did_you_know.en: In 1969 two men claimed to have shot at Morag after their boat struck it on Loch Morar.

short_description.id: Graoully adalah naga legenda Metz yang tinggal di amfiteater Romawi dan meracuni kota sampai dikalahkan Santo Klemens, uskup pertama Metz.
short_description.en: Graoully is a legendary dragon of Metz that lived in the Roman amphitheatre and poisoned the city until Saint Clement, its first bishop, overcame it.

long_description.id: Graoully adalah naga dalam cerita rakyat Metz yang tinggal di amfiteater Romawi bersama banyak ular; napas berbisa mereka membuat kota tak bisa dimasuki. Santo Klemens mengangkat salib, mengikat Graoully dengan stolanya, dan menuntunnya ke Sungai Seille, tempat menurut satu versi monster itu ditelan bumi; versi lain menyebut Klemens menusuknya dengan tombak. Versi pertama legenda ini dari akhir abad ke-10 dan melambangkan kemenangan Kristen atas paganisme.
long_description.en: Graoully is a dragon of Metz folklore that lived in the Roman amphitheatre with many serpents whose venomous breath sealed off the city. Saint Clement raised his cross, bound Graoully with his stole and led it to the River Seille, where in one version the earth swallowed it; other versions have him spear it. The legend's first version dates from the late 10th century and symbolises Christianity's victory over paganism.

long_description.id: Namanya mungkin dari grouiller, "berkerumun", atau dari bahasa Jerman gräulich, "mengerikan". Patungnya diarak di Metz sampai abad ke-19, nama Rue Taison dikaitkan dengan peringatan tentangnya, dan ia menjadi lambang kota serta klub FC Metz sampai 2021.
long_description.en: Its name may come from grouiller, 'to swarm', or German gräulich, 'horrible'. Its effigy was paraded in Metz until the 19th century, the Rue Taison is linked to a warning about it, and it became a city symbol and the FC Metz emblem until 2021.

short_description.id: Guajona adalah nenek bertudung hitam dari tradisi Cantabria yang pada malam hari mengisap darah anak-anak yang tidur dengan satu giginya yang panjang.
short_description.en: The Guajona is a black-hooded hag of the tradition of Cantabria who sucks the blood of sleeping children at night with her single long tooth.

long_description.id: Guajona atau Lumia adalah monster dari tradisi lisan Cantabria, nenek kurus berjubah hitam berkaki burung, berwajah kuning berkutil, bermata kecil berkilau, dengan satu gigi hitam panjang sampai bawah dagu. Ia hanya keluar pada malam hari, diam-diam masuk ke rumah, dan mengisap darah anak serta remaja yang tidur tanpa membunuh mereka, sehingga mereka bangun lemah dan pucat.
long_description.en: The Guajona or Lumia is a monster of the oral tradition of Cantabria, a thin black-cloaked hag with bird's feet, a yellow warty face, small bright eyes and one long black tooth reaching below her chin. She only comes out at night, slips into houses and drinks the blood of sleeping children and youths without killing them, so they wake weak and pale.

long_description.id: Ia salah satu dari sedikit mitos vampir Spanyol; sumber berbeda apakah ia juga menyerang orang dewasa. Namanya bentuk pembesar dari Guaja (Asturias: Guaxa), mungkin dari bahasa Arab wahsh, "binatang buas", atau dari bahasa Latin hostem, "musuh". Miguel de Unamuno pernah mengutipnya.
long_description.en: She is one of Spain's few vampire myths; sources differ on whether she also attacks adults. Her name is an augmentative of Guaja (Asturian Guaxa), perhaps from Arabic wahsh, 'wild beast', or from Latin hostem, 'enemy'. Miguel de Unamuno quoted her.

short_description.id: Alp adalah makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang menindih dada orang tidur dan menimbulkan mimpi buruk; ia pandai berganti rupa dan memakai topi ajaib Tarnkappe.
short_description.en: The Alp is a supernatural being of German folklore that sits on sleepers' chests and causes nightmares; it is a skilled shapeshifter that wears a magic Tarnkappe hat.

long_description.id: Alp adalah makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang kadang disamakan dengan vampir, tetapi perilakunya lebih mirip inkubus. Kata Alp adalah bentuk Jerman dari kata yang dalam bahasa Inggris menjadi elf; ia juga dikenal sebagai trud, mar, mahr, schrat, dan walrider. Artikel bahasa Jerman menyebutnya Nachtalb, sebutan belakangan untuk makhluk yang semula bernama Mahr, yang menindih manusia pada malam hari dan menebar kengerian.
long_description.en: The Alp is a supernatural being of German folklore sometimes likened to a vampire, though its behaviour is closer to an incubus. Alp is the German form of the word that became English elf; it is also known as trud, mar, mahr, schrat and walrider. The German article calls it Nachtalb, a late name for a being originally called Mahr that weighs on people at night and fills them with dread.

long_description.id: Alp biasanya jantan dan menyerang korban, kerap perempuan, pada malam hari dengan mengendalikan mimpi mereka. Serangannya disebut Alpdruck: ia duduk di dada orang tidur dan makin berat hingga korban terbangun ketakutan, sesak napas, dan tak bisa bergerak. Alp juga dikatakan mengasamkan susu, mengusutkan rambut menjadi "simpul elf", dan menunggangi kuda sampai kelelahan.
long_description.en: The Alp is usually male and attacks its victims, often women, at night by controlling their dreams. Its attack is called Alpdruck: it sits on the sleeper's chest and grows heavier until the victim wakes terrified, breathless and unable to move. Alpe are also said to sour milk, tangle hair into 'elf-knots' and ride horses to exhaustion.

long_description.id: Alp terkenal karena kemampuannya berubah menjadi kucing, babi, anjing, ular, atau kupu-kupu putih kecil. Ia selalu memakai topi yang disebut Tarnkappe, yang memberinya kekuatan gaib dan membuatnya tak terlihat; Alp yang kehilangan topi itu akan menawarkan imbalan besar untuk pengembaliannya. Perlindungan terhadapnya antara lain sapu di bawah bantal, ladam besi di tiang ranjang, cermin di dada, baja, dan salib, serta menyumbat lubang kunci sebelum ia datang.
long_description.en: The Alp is known for turning into a cat, pig, dog, snake or small white butterfly. It always wears a hat called the Tarnkappe that gives it magic powers and invisibility; an Alp that loses the hat will offer a great reward for its return. Protections include a broomstick under the pillow, iron horseshoes on the bedpost, a mirror on the chest, steel and crosses, and stopping up keyholes before it comes.

long_description.id: Seorang anak bisa menjadi Alp bila ibunya menggigit kekang kuda untuk meredakan sakit saat persalinan yang sangat lama, atau bila ia lahir berselaput atau berambut di telapak tangan; bayi lahir mati juga diduga kembali sebagai Alp. Menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, Alp biasanya makhluk kecil hitam yang masuk lewat lubang kunci atau lubang dahan.
long_description.en: A child may become an Alp if its mother bites a horse collar to ease an extremely long childbirth, or if it is born with a caul or hair on its palms; stillborn infants are also suspected of returning as Alpe. According to the German article, the Alp is usually a small black being that enters through keyholes or knot-holes.

statement.id: Anak bisa menjadi Alp bila ibunya menggigit kekang kuda untuk meredakan sakit persalinan yang sangat lama, atau bila lahir berselaput atau berambut di telapak tangan; bayi lahir mati juga diduga kembali dari kubur sebagai Alp.
statement.en: A child may become an Alp if the mother bites a horse collar during an extremely long childbirth, or if born with a caul or hair on the palms; stillborn infants are suspected of returning from the grave as Alpe.

statement.en: It is usually a small black being that attacks sleeping people and domestic animals, rarely objects, and enters through keyholes or knot-holes.

statement.en: In Germanic folk belief an Alb is a low-ranking subterranean nature spirit; Alben are elf-like beings close to kobolds and dwarves.

claims.quote: The Alp, in many cases, is considered a demon, but there have been some instances in which the Alp is created from the spirits of recently dead relatives, more akin to a spirit or ghost.

short_description.id: Guivre atau vouivre adalah naga berwujud ular bernapas racun dari legenda Prancis abad pertengahan, agresif tetapi takut pada manusia telanjang.
short_description.en: The guivre or vouivre is a serpentine, venom-breathing dragon of medieval French legend, aggressive yet afraid of naked humans.

long_description.id: Guivre, givre, atau vouivre adalah nama Prancis untuk makhluk mitis berwujud ular yang setara dengan lindworm atau wyvern; namanya berasal dari kata Latin vipera, dan kata Inggris wyvern berasal darinya. Ia bertubuh panjang seperti ular dan berkepala naga, kadang bertanduk, bernapas racun, dan tinggal di kolam, danau, hutan, dan tempat lembap. Ia sangat agresif tetapi tersipu dan memalingkan muka bila melihat manusia telanjang.
long_description.en: Guivre, givre or vouivre is the French name for a serpentine mythical creature equivalent to a lindworm or wyvern; the name comes from Latin vipera, and English wyvern comes from it. It has a long serpentine body and dragon's head, sometimes horns, venomous breath, and lives in pools, lakes, forests and damp places. It is highly aggressive yet blushes and looks away on seeing a naked human.

long_description.id: Dalam heraldik vouivre disebut guivre, dan di Lorraine, Bourgogne, Franche-Comté, Jura, serta Swiss ia naga berkaki dua atau ular bersayap yang membawa batu merah delima di dahinya. Dalam kisah Santo Samson dari Dol, Santo Suliao mengeluarkan seekor guivre kecil dari jubah imam yang tamak, lalu mengusirnya.
long_description.en: In heraldry the vouivre is called guivre, and in Lorraine, Burgundy, Franche-Comté, the Jura and Switzerland it is a two-legged dragon or winged serpent bearing a carbuncle on its brow. In the tale of Samson of Dol, Saint Suliao pulls a small guivre from a greedy priest's robe and exorcises it.

description.id: Guivre bernapas racun.
description.en: The guivre has venomous breath.

description.id: Guivre takut pada manusia telanjang dan memalingkan muka.
description.en: The guivre fears naked humans and looks away.

summary.id: Seekor guivre muncul di jubah imam yang menyembunyikan roti, lalu diusir oleh Santo Suliao.
summary.en: A guivre appears in the robe of a priest who hid bread and is exorcised by Saint Suliao.

note.en: The word wyvern comes from vouivre.

claims.quote: Guivre (or givre) and vouivre are French names for a type of serpentine mythical creature, by extension a dragon, by some accords, equivalent to a lindworm or wyvern.

statement.en: Guivre (or givre) and vouivre are French names for a serpentine mythical creature, by extension a dragon, by some accounts equivalent to a lindworm or wyvern.

claims.quote: In legend they are portrayed as serpentine creatures who possessed venomous breath and prowled the countryside of Medieval France.

statement.id: Dalam legenda mereka digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip ular bernapas racun yang berkeliaran di pedesaan Prancis abad pertengahan.
statement.en: In legend they are serpentine creatures with venomous breath that prowled the countryside of medieval France.

claims.quote: The English wyvern (a type of dragon) derives from Old French "vouivre".

statement.id: Kata Inggris wyvern berasal dari kata Prancis Kuno vouivre.
statement.en: The English word wyvern derives from Old French vouivre.

claims.quote: Guivres (alternatively givres) were said to possess a long, serpentine body and a dragon's head. The hind feet are not as visible if present at all. The guivre had horns in its forehead in some accounts, as well.

statement.id: Guivre bertubuh panjang seperti ular dan berkepala naga, kaki belakangnya hampir tak terlihat kalaupun ada, dan dalam sebagian kisah bertanduk di dahi.
statement.en: Guivres had a long serpentine body and a dragon's head, hind feet barely visible if present at all, and in some accounts horns on the forehead.

claims.quote: Locally in France, it was known as an extremely aggressive creature that would sometimes attack without being provoked. They were afraid of naked humans, and when saw them, blushed and looked away.

statement.id: Di Prancis ia dikenal sangat agresif dan kadang menyerang tanpa sebab, tetapi takut pada manusia telanjang: bila melihatnya, guivre tersipu dan memalingkan muka.
statement.en: Locally in France it was known as extremely aggressive, sometimes attacking unprovoked, yet it feared naked humans and would blush and look away on seeing one.

claims.quote: Documentation points to their residence as being in small bodies of water like pools and lakes, forests, and any damp place.

statement.id: Guivre tinggal di perairan kecil seperti kolam dan danau, di hutan, dan di tempat lembap.
statement.en: Guivres lived in small bodies of water like pools and lakes, in forests and in any damp place.

claims.quote: Samson of Dol was present at an encounter between a small dragon-like creature, known as La Guivre ("the guivre"), and a priest.

statement.id: Santo Samson dari Dol menyaksikan pertemuan seorang imam dengan makhluk kecil mirip naga yang disebut La Guivre.
statement.en: Samson of Dol witnessed an encounter between a priest and a small dragon-like creature called La Guivre.

claims.quote: He admonished the priest and removed a hideous serpentine creature from the robe. There, he exorcised it and then compelled another man to throw it from the roof of a building in Garot.

statement.id: Santo Suliao menegur imam yang menyembunyikan roti di jubahnya, mengeluarkan makhluk ular yang mengerikan dari jubah itu, mengusirnya, lalu menyuruh orang lain melemparkannya dari atap sebuah bangunan di Garot.
statement.en: Saint Suliao rebuked the priest who had hidden bread in his robe, pulled a hideous serpentine creature from it, exorcised it and had another man throw it from a roof in Garot.

claims.quote: La vouivre est une créature légendaire présente dans plusieurs pays européens, ayant généralement la forme d'un dragon bipède ou d'un serpent ailé. Elle est souvent censée porter une escarboucle sur le front. En héraldique, elle est aussi appelée guivre.

statement.en: According to the French article, the vouivre is a legendary creature of several European countries, usually a two-legged dragon or winged serpent often bearing a carbuncle on its brow, called guivre in heraldry.

claims.quote: Ce mot est un régionalisme linguistique propre à la Lorraine, la Bourgogne, la Franche-Comté, le Jura et la Suisse.

short_description.id: Hercinia adalah burung legendaris dari Hutan Hercynia yang bulunya bersinar seperti api pada malam hari, dicatat Plinius Tua dan bestiari abad pertengahan.
short_description.en: The hercinia is a legendary bird of the Hercynian Forest whose feathers shine like fire at night, recorded by Pliny the Elder and the medieval bestiaries.

long_description.id: Hercinia adalah burung legendaris Hutan Hercynia di Germania kuno. Plinius Tua pada abad ke-1 menulis bahwa bulunya bersinar seperti api pada malam hari, dan pada abad ke-7 Isidorus dari Sevilla menyebut bulu yang diletakkan di tanah memancarkan cahaya penunjuk jalan. Ia digambarkan dalam bestiari abad pertengahan.
long_description.en: The hercinia is a legendary bird of the Hercynian Forest of ancient Germany. In the 1st century Pliny the Elder wrote that its feathers shine like fire at night, and in the 7th century Isidore of Seville said feathers laid on the ground give light to show the way. It appears in medieval bestiaries.

long_description.id: Laporan ini mungkin berasal dari burung berbulu warna-warni yang memantulkan cahaya bulan, seperti burung hantu serak. Legenda ini mengilhami puisi Thomas Moore A Dream of Antiquity.
long_description.en: The reports may come from iridescent birds reflecting moonlight, such as the barn owl. The legend inspired Thomas Moore's poem A Dream of Antiquity.

origin.en: Pliny the Elder and the bestiaries.

description.id: Hutan kuno tempat hercinia tinggal.
description.en: The ancient forest where the hercinia lived.

claims.quote: Hercinia is a legendary bird with glowing feathers that inhabited the Hercynian Forest of ancient Germany.

statement.id: Hercinia adalah burung legendaris berbulu bercahaya yang menghuni Hutan Hercynia di Germania kuno.
statement.en: The hercinia is a legendary bird with glowing feathers that lived in the Hercynian Forest of ancient Germany.

claims.quote: The hercinia is depicted in Medieval bestiaries and was recorded in the 1st century by Pliny the Elder, who wrote, "In the Hercynian Forest, in Germany, we hear of a singular kind of bird, the feathers of which shine at night like fire".

statement.id: Hercinia digambarkan dalam bestiari Abad Pertengahan dan dicatat pada abad ke-1 oleh Plinius Tua: "Di Hutan Hercynia, di Germania, terdengar kabar tentang sejenis burung aneh yang bulunya bersinar seperti api pada malam hari."
statement.en: The hercinia appears in Medieval bestiaries and was recorded in the 1st century by Pliny the Elder: 'In the Hercynian Forest, in Germany, we hear of a singular kind of bird, the feathers of which shine at night like fire.'

claims.quote: Writing in the 7th century, Isidore of Seville notes, "Their feathers sparkle so much in the shade that, however dark the night is with thick shadows, these feathers, when placed on the ground, give off light that helps to mark the way, and the sign of the glittering feathers makes clear the direction of the path".

statement.id: Pada abad ke-7 Isidorus dari Sevilla menulis bahwa bulunya begitu berkilau sehingga, segelap apa pun malam, bulu yang diletakkan di tanah memancarkan cahaya penunjuk jalan.
statement.en: Writing in the 7th century, Isidore of Seville notes that its feathers sparkle so that, however dark the night, feathers laid on the ground give off light that marks the path.

claims.quote: It is possible that the reports of the hercinia were based on sightings of birds with iridescent feathers that reflected moonlight, a phenomenon that has been reported of a number of species of birds, including the barn owl and the bittern.

statement.id: Laporan tentang hercinia mungkin berasal dari burung berbulu warna-warni yang memantulkan cahaya bulan, gejala yang dilaporkan pada beberapa spesies seperti burung hantu serak dan burung bittern.
statement.en: Reports of the hercinia may come from birds with iridescent feathers reflecting moonlight, as reported of several species including the barn owl and the bittern.

claims.quote: La légende de ces oiseaux lumineux présents dans la forêt Hercynienne a inspiré de nombreuses œuvres d’art, notamment le célèbre poème de Thomas Moore : A Dream of Antiquity.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, legenda burung bercahaya ini mengilhami banyak karya seni, termasuk puisi Thomas Moore A Dream of Antiquity.
statement.en: According to the French article, the legend inspired many works of art, notably Thomas Moore's poem A Dream of Antiquity.

claims.quote: Ellos se encontraban en el bosque Hercínico, en el sur de Alemania, donde sus plumas brillantes mantenían sendas encendidas en la espesura del bosque.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, burung-burung ini tinggal di Hutan Hercynia di Jerman selatan, tempat bulu bercahayanya menerangi jalan setapak di hutan lebat.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, they lived in the Hercynian Forest in southern Germany, where their glowing feathers lit the paths through the thick forest.

short_description.id: Herensuge adalah naga atau ular raksasa mitologi Basque, sering berkepala tujuh, yang tinggal di gua dan menuntut korban sampai dikalahkan Santo Mikael atau seorang pahlawan.
short_description.en: Herensuge is the dragon or giant serpent of Basque mythology, often seven-headed, that lives in caves and demands victims until Saint Michael or a hero defeats it.

long_description.id: Herensuge adalah naga mitologi Basque yang sering berwujud ular; namanya beragam tetapi selalu berakhiran suge, "ular". Ia kadang berkepala tujuh, yang dipercaya anak-anaknya sendiri, dan menurut sebagian sumber dapat terbang. Ia menghuni gua, gunung, dan jurang, menarik manusia dan hewan ke guanya dengan napasnya, dan meneror gembala.
long_description.en: Herensuge is the Basque dragon, often in serpent form; its names vary but always end in suge, 'snake'. It sometimes has seven heads, thought to be its own offspring, and some sources say it can fly. It lives in caves, mountains and chasms, draws people and animals into its lair with its breath, and terrorises shepherds.

long_description.id: Dalam legenda Aralar, ksatria Teodosio de Goñi yang sedang menebus dosa diselamatkan Santo Mikael, yang datang bersama Allah dan memenggal naga itu; kisah ini terkait biara San Miguel de Aralar dan peralihan ke agama Kristen. Dalam dongeng lain, seorang pangeran membunuh Herensuge berkepala tujuh dengan bantuan raksasa bermata satu Tartalo.
long_description.en: In the Aralar legend, the penitent knight Teodosio de Goñi is saved by Saint Michael, who comes with God and beheads the dragon; the tale is tied to the monastery of San Miguel de Aralar and the turn to Christianity. In another tale a prince kills the seven-headed Herensuge with the help of the one-eyed giant Tartalo.

who.id: Naga atau ular raksasa berkepala tujuh.

famous_for.en: Defeated by Saint Michael at Aralar.

role.en: The dragon beheaded by Saint Michael.

summary.id: Ksatria Teodosio de Goñi menyelamatkan perempuan tebusan naga di Aralar; ketika terdesak ia berdoa, dan Santo Mikael datang bersama Allah memenggal naga itu.
summary.en: The knight Teodosio de Goñi rescues the dragon's ransomed woman at Aralar; cornered, he prays, and Saint Michael comes with God and beheads the dragon.

description.id: Biara yang terkait legenda Teodosio.
description.en: The monastery tied to the Teodosio legend.

note.en: The god linked with it.
The giant who helps a prince kill it.

claims.quote: Herensuge is the name for a mythical dragon in the Basque language. In Basque mythology, dragons appear sparingly, sometimes with seven heads. Herensuge often also appear in the form of a serpent.

statement.id: Herensuge adalah nama naga mitis dalam bahasa Basque; dalam mitologi Basque naga jarang muncul, kadang berkepala tujuh, dan Herensuge sering juga berwujud ular.
statement.en: Herensuge is the Basque name for a mythical dragon; dragons appear rarely in Basque mythology, sometimes with seven heads, and Herensuge often also takes the form of a serpent.

claims.quote: The seven heads were believed to be the offspring of the Herensuge dragon. When the little dragons were fully grown, they would fall off their mother's head.

statement.id: Ketujuh kepala itu dipercaya anak-anak Herensuge; setelah dewasa, naga-naga kecil itu lepas dari kepala induknya.
statement.en: The seven heads were believed to be the Herensuge's offspring; when grown, the little dragons fell off their mother's head.

statement.id: Hanya dewa Sugaar yang dikaitkan dengan makhluk ini, meski lebih sering dengan ular.
statement.en: Only the god Sugaar is linked with this creature, though more often with a serpent.

statement.en: According to the German article it is a devilish cave spirit appearing as a serpent, with seven heads and able to fly, though sources differ on this.

claims.quote: Mit seinem Atem lockt er Menschen und Tiere in seine Höhle, um sie zu verschlingen.

statement.id: Dengan napasnya ia menarik manusia dan hewan ke guanya untuk dilahap.
statement.en: With its breath it draws people and animals into its cave to devour them.

claims.quote: Herensuge habite cavernes, montagnes et gouffres, et ses attaques terrifient les bergers et troupeaux ; il est au centre de nombreux récits héroïques.

statement.id: Herensuge menghuni gua, gunung, dan jurang, serangannya menakutkan gembala dan ternak, dan ia menjadi pusat banyak kisah kepahlawanan.
statement.en: Herensuge lives in caves, mountains and chasms, its attacks terrify shepherds and flocks, and it is at the heart of many heroic tales.

statement.en: Its names vary, but the constant suffix suge ('snake') shows its serpent nature.

statement.en: Other names include Erensugue, Iraunsuge, Lerensuge, Herainsuge, Errensuge, Edensugue and Igensuge.

claims.quote: A legend describes a Navarrese knight, Teodosio de Goñi, who while making penance for double parricide in the Aralar Range rescues a woman that had been given as ransom to the dragon.

statement.id: Sebuah legenda menceritakan ksatria Navarra Teodosio de Goñi, yang saat menjalani penebusan dosa karena membunuh kedua orang tuanya di Pegunungan Aralar menyelamatkan seorang perempuan yang diserahkan sebagai tebusan kepada naga.
statement.en: A legend tells of the Navarrese knight Teodosio de Goñi who, doing penance in the Aralar range for killing both parents, rescues a woman given to the dragon as ransom.

claims.quote: the knight prays to Saint Michael to save him. In Heaven, the archangel is notified, but refuses to enter the fight without God. The archangel arrives with God over his head and decapitates the dragon, liberating Teodosio from his chains and ending his penance.

statement.id: Ksatria itu berdoa kepada Santo Mikael; sang malaikat agung menolak bertarung tanpa Allah, lalu datang dengan Allah di atas kepalanya, memenggal naga itu, dan membebaskan Teodosio dari rantai serta penebusannya.
statement.en: The knight prays to Saint Michael; the archangel refuses to fight without God, then arrives with God above his head, beheads the dragon and frees Teodosio from his chains and his penance.

claims.quote: This legend is associated to the monastery of San Miguel de Aralar. It has been interpreted as a way of justifying the break from the religion and customs of pagan Basques and the adoption of Christianity and, specifically, the veneration for St. Michael.

statement.en: The legend is tied to the monastery of San Miguel de Aralar and has been read as justifying the shift from pagan Basque religion to Christianity, especially the cult of St Michael.

short_description.id: Glashtyn adalah makhluk legenda cerita rakyat Manx, goblin yang keluar dari air atau berwujud kuda muda, kadang disamakan dengan kuda air cabbyl-ushtey.
short_description.en: The glashtyn is a legendary creature of Manx folklore, a goblin that comes out of the water or takes the shape of a colt, sometimes equated with the water horse cabbyl-ushtey.

long_description.id: Glashtyn (Inggris Manx/Manx English: glashtin, glashtan, atau glashan; Manx: glashtin atau glashtyn) adalah makhluk legenda dari cerita rakyat Manx. Glashtin dikatakan goblin yang keluar dari habitat airnya untuk berhubungan dengan penduduk pulau; yang lain mengatakan ia berwujud kuda muda, atau menyamakannya dengan kuda air setempat cabbyl-ushtey, dan satu sumber menyebutnya banteng air (tarroo-ushtey), setengah sapi setengah kuda. Kata glashtin diduga berasal dari kata Kelt (Celtic) glais, "sungai kecil" atau kadang laut.
long_description.en: The glashtyn (Manx English glashtin, glashtan or glashan; Manx glashtin or glashtyn) is a legendary being of Manx folklore. The glashtin is said to be a goblin that leaves its watery home to mix with the islanders; others say it takes the form of a colt, or equate it with the local water horse cabbyl-ushtey, and one source makes it a water-bull (tarroo-ushtey), half cow and half horse. The word glashtin is thought to come from Celtic glais, 'stream', or at times the sea.

long_description.id: Beberapa kisah menuturkan ia mengejar perempuan, yang lolos dengan memotong ujung roknya; dalam satu versi modern perempuan itu selamat berkat kokok ayam jantan, dan glashtin yang menyamar sebagai lelaki tampan terbongkar oleh telinga kudanya. Kamus Moore (1924) mengartikan glashan sebagai "goblin berbulu". Menurut artikel fr, Alastyn atau Glashtyn hanya keluar pada malam hari dan dapat berwujud anak kuda kelabu; dalam wujud manusia ia pemuda sangat tampan bermata berkilau, berkulit gelap, dan berambut ikal, hanya dapat dikenali dari telinganya yang runcing seperti telinga kuda.
long_description.en: Some tales tell of it chasing women, who escape by cutting free the hem of their skirts; in one modern version the woman is saved by a cock's crowing, and the glashtin, posing as a handsome man, is betrayed by his horse's ears. Moore's dictionary (1924) glosses glashan as 'hairy goblin'. According to the fr article the Alastyn or Glashtyn comes out only at night and can take the shape of a grey colt; in human form it is a very handsome young man with shining eyes, dark skin and curly hair, known only by its ears, pointed like a horse's.

did_you_know.id: Glashtyn yang menyamar sebagai lelaki tampan dapat dikenali dari telinganya yang tetap runcing seperti telinga kuda.
did_you_know.en: A glashtyn disguised as a handsome man can be recognised by its ears, which stay pointed like a horse's.

short_description.id: Hiiden hirvi adalah rusa besar mitos dalam mitologi Finlandia yang harus diburu dengan ski; mitosnya menceritakan asal-usul ski dan rusa besar.
short_description.en: Hiiden hirvi is a mythical moose of Finnish mythology that must be hunted on skis; its myth tells the origin of skis and of the moose.

long_description.id: Hiiden hirvi, "rusa besar milik Hiisi", adalah rusa besar mitos dalam mitologi Finlandia yang harus diburu dengan bermain ski; mitosnya menceritakan penciptaan ski dan asal-usul rusa besar. Dalam epos Kalevala ia hewan gaib yang sulit ditangkap, cepat, dan kuat, dan Louhi menugaskan para pelamar putrinya menangkapnya hidup-hidup. Padanannya di Estonia adalah Hiiehobune, "kuda milik Hiis".
long_description.en: Hiiden hirvi, "Hiisi's moose", is a mythical moose of Finnish mythology that must be hunted on skis; its myth tells the creation of skis and the origin of the moose. In the Kalevala epic it is a supernatural animal, hard to catch, swift and strong, and Louhi sets her daughters' suitors the task of catching it alive. Its Estonian counterpart is Hiiehobune, "Hiis's horse".

long_description.id: Dalam versi Karelia Putih dan Olonets, sang tokoh tiba di tempat perempuan tertawa, anak-anak menangis, dan anjing menggonggong karena rusa itu baru lewat dan merusak makanan, lalu memburunya hingga skinya patah dan rusa itu lolos. Dalam versi Karelia Ladoga tokohnya biasanya seorang Sami bernama Lauri, dan dalam satu versi Väinämöinen berhasil memburunya.
long_description.en: In White Karelian and Olonets versions the hero reaches a place where women laugh, children cry and dogs bark because the moose has just passed and spoiled the food, then chases it until a ski breaks and it escapes. In Ladoga Karelian versions the hero is usually a Sámi named Lauri, and in one version Väinämöinen succeeds in the hunt.

short_description.id: Hafgufa adalah makhluk laut raksasa dalam sastra Nordik yang konon menghuni perairan Islandia dan begitu besar sehingga lebih mirip pulau daripada makhluk hidup.
short_description.en: Hafgufa is a giant sea creature of Norse literature said to inhabit Iceland's waters, so huge that it looked more like an island than a living thing.

long_description.id: Hafgufa (dari kata Nordik Kuno haf, "laut", dan gufa, "uap") adalah makhluk laut yang konon menghuni perairan Islandia, yaitu Laut Greenland, hingga ke selatan menuju Helluland. Ia disebut dalam risalah Norwegia abad ke-13 Konungs skuggsjá ("Cermin Raja") dan dalam daftar paus (þulur) di Snorra Edda.
long_description.en: Hafgufa (from Old Norse haf, 'sea', and gufa, 'steam') is a sea creature said to live in Iceland's waters, the Greenland Sea, and southward toward Helluland. It is mentioned in the 13th-century Norwegian tract Konungs skuggsjá ('King's Mirror') and in the list of whales (þulur) in the Snorra Edda.

long_description.id: Dalam Konungs skuggsjá, sang raja menggambarkannya sebagai ikan raksasa yang lebih mirip pulau, jarang terlihat dan selalu di dua tempat yang sama, sehingga ia menduga hanya ada dua ekor yang mandul. Makhluk itu bersendawa mengeluarkan makanan yang menarik ikan-ikan, lalu menutup mulut dan menelan semuanya sekaligus.
long_description.en: In the Konungs skuggsjá the king describes it as a huge fish more like an island, rarely seen and always in the same two places, so he guessed there were only two and that they were barren. It would belch up food that drew in fish, then shut its mouth and swallow them all at once.

long_description.id: Dalam versi akhir Örvar-Odds saga dari akhir abad ke-14, hafgufa adalah monster laut terbesar yang memangsa paus, kapal, dan manusia; awak kapal dalam saga itu berlayar di antara lubang hidung dan rahang bawahnya, yang mereka kira dua batu besar. Penelitian menduga kisah ini berasal dari teknik makan paus yang disebut trap-feeding, sedangkan Uskup Gunnerus dari Trondheim menganggapnya kraken itu sendiri.
long_description.en: In the later version of Örvar-Odds saga from the late 14th century, hafgufa is the largest sea monster, eating whales, ships and men; the saga's crew sailed between its nostril and lower jaw, which the crew took for two great rocks. Research suggests the stories arose from a whale feeding technique called trap-feeding, while Bishop Gunnerus of Trondheim held it to be the kraken itself.

short_description.id: Hircocervus atau tragelaphos adalah makhluk khayalan setengah kambing setengah rusa yang dipakai Platon dan Aristoteles sebagai contoh sesuatu yang dapat dibayangkan tetapi tidak ada.
short_description.en: The hircocervus or tragelaph is an imaginary half-goat, half-stag that Plato and Aristotle used as an example of something imaginable but non-existent.

long_description.id: Hircocervus, dari bahasa Latin hircus "kambing jantan" dan cervus "rusa jantan", atau tragelaphos dalam bahasa Yunani, adalah makhluk khayalan setengah kambing setengah rusa. Dalam Republik, Sokrates menyamakan pemikirannya dengan pelukis kambing-rusa, dan Aristoteles memakainya sebagai contoh hal yang dapat dijelaskan tetapi tidak ada; Boethius menerjemahkannya menjadi hircocervus. Diodorus Siculus justru menganggapnya hewan nyata.
long_description.en: The hircocervus, from Latin hircus 'billy goat' and cervus 'stag', or tragelaphos in Greek, is an imaginary half-goat, half-stag. In the Republic Socrates compares his thinking to painters of goat-stags, and Aristotle used it as an example of something describable yet non-existent; Boethius translated it as hircocervus. Diodorus Siculus, though, treated it as a real animal.

long_description.id: Kata ini masuk bahasa Inggris pada 1398, dipakai Martin Luther pada 1540 untuk hukum yang tidak menghukum, dan kemudian menjadi kiasan untuk hal yang mustahil. Buffon mengenali tragelaphos Plinius sebagai rusa tua bersurai panjang.
long_description.en: The word entered English in 1398, was used by Martin Luther in 1540 for a law that does not condemn, and later became a figure for anything absurd. Buffon identified Pliny's tragelaph as an old long-maned stag.

origin.id: Filsafat Yunani dan naskah abad pertengahan.

claims.quote: The hircocervus (Latin: hircus, "billy goat" + cervus, "stag") or tragelaph (Greek: τράγος, romanized: tragos, "billy goat" + έλαφος, elaphos, "stag"), also known as a goat-stag, was a legendary creature imagined to be half-goat, half-stag.

statement.id: Hircocervus (Latin: hircus, "kambing jantan" + cervus, "rusa jantan") atau tragelaphos (Yunani), juga disebut kambing-rusa, adalah makhluk legendaris yang dibayangkan setengah kambing setengah rusa.
statement.en: The hircocervus (Latin hircus, 'billy goat' + cervus, 'stag') or tragelaph (Greek), also called goat-stag, was a legendary creature imagined as half goat, half stag.

claims.quote: In Plato's Republic, Socrates speaks of his own image-making as similar to that of painters who paint goat-stags, combining the features of different things together (488a).

statement.id: Dalam Republik karya Platon, Sokrates menyamakan caranya membuat gambaran dengan pelukis yang melukis kambing-rusa, menggabungkan ciri berbagai hal (488a).
statement.en: In Plato's Republic, Socrates likens his image-making to painters who paint goat-stags by combining features of different things (488a).

claims.quote: In his work De Interpretatione, Aristotle utilized the idea of a fabulous goat-stag to express the philosophical concept of something that is describable even though it does not really exist. His Greek "τραγέλαφος" was rendered into Latin "hircocervus" by Boethius.

statement.id: Dalam De Interpretatione, Aristoteles memakai kambing-rusa dongeng untuk menjelaskan konsep sesuatu yang dapat dijelaskan walau tidak benar-benar ada; Boethius menerjemahkan kata Yunaninya menjadi hircocervus.
statement.en: In De Interpretatione Aristotle used the fabulous goat-stag to express something describable though non-existent; Boethius rendered his Greek word into Latin as hircocervus.

claims.quote: On the other hand, Diodorus Siculus treats the tragelaphos as an existing animal, and there are references in Greek literature to other hybrid creatures such as the hippelaphos (horse-stag).

statement.id: Sebaliknya, Diodorus Siculus memperlakukan tragelaphos sebagai hewan yang benar-benar ada, dan sastra Yunani juga menyebut hibrida lain seperti hippelaphos (kuda-rusa).
statement.en: Diodorus Siculus, by contrast, treats the tragelaphos as a real animal, and Greek literature mentions other hybrids such as the hippelaphos (horse-stag).

claims.quote: The word hircocervus first appears in the English language in a medieval manuscript dating from 1398 (now at the Bodleian Library).

statement.id: Kata hircocervus pertama muncul dalam bahasa Inggris pada naskah abad pertengahan tahun 1398 yang kini di Bodleian Library.
statement.en: The word hircocervus first appears in English in a medieval manuscript of 1398, now in the Bodleian Library.

claims.quote: Martin Luther uses the term "tragelaphus" in his Theses Against the Antinomians (1540, Sixth Set) to describe "a law that does not condemn".

statement.id: Martin Luther memakai istilah tragelaphus dalam Tesis Melawan Kaum Antinomian (1540) untuk menggambarkan "hukum yang tidak menghukum".
statement.en: Martin Luther used 'tragelaphus' in his Theses Against the Antinomians (1540) for 'a law that does not condemn'.

claims.quote: Quant à Pline, il parle d'un tragélaphe qui est sans doute le même animal. Buffon a reconnu sous ces deux noms un vieux cerf dont le cou finit par se couvrir de longs crins et le fait ressembler de loin à un cheval.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, Plinius menyebut tragelaphos yang mungkin hewan yang sama dengan hippelaphos Aristoteles, dan Buffon mengenalinya sebagai rusa tua yang lehernya tertutup surai panjang sehingga dari jauh mirip kuda.
statement.en: According to the French article, Pliny's tragelaph is probably the same as Aristotle's hippelaphos, and Buffon identified both as an old stag whose neck grows long hair so that from afar it looks like a horse.

claims.quote: Col tempo l'uso letterale del termine è stato abbandonato in favore di quello metaforico per riferirsi a cose assurde ed irreali.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Italia, lama-kelamaan istilah ini dipakai secara kiasan untuk hal yang mustahil dan tidak nyata.
statement.en: According to the Italian article, the term came to be used figuratively for absurd and unreal things.

short_description.id: Hamingja adalah roh pelindung perempuan dalam mitologi Nordik yang menyertai seseorang dan menentukan nasib baik serta kebahagiaannya, lalu diwariskan dalam keluarga.
short_description.en: The hamingja is a female guardian spirit of Norse mythology that accompanies a person, decides their luck and happiness, and passes down within a family.

long_description.id: Hamingja adalah jenis roh pelindung perempuan dalam mitologi Nordik yang diyakini menyertai seseorang dan menentukan untung serta kebahagiaannya; karena itu kata ini juga berarti kebahagiaan, makna yang dipakai dalam bahasa Islandia modern. Saat orang itu meninggal, hamingja beralih kepada anggota keluarga tercinta sehingga dapat menyertai satu keluarga turun-temurun.
long_description.en: The hamingja is a kind of female guardian spirit in Norse mythology believed to accompany a person and decide their fortune and happiness; for that reason the word also came to mean happiness, its sense in modern Icelandic. When the person died, the hamingja went to a beloved relative and could thus follow a family over generations.

long_description.id: Hamingja bahkan bisa dipinjamkan: Hjalti Skeggiason, sebelum berlayar dalam perjalanan berbahaya, meminta Olaf II dari Norwegia meminjamkan hamingja-nya. Ia biasanya muncul dalam tidur berwujud hewan, dan bisa juga merupakan roh orang yang sedang tidur dalam rupa hewan, seperti Bödvar Bjarki dalam saga Hrólfr Kraki.
long_description.en: A hamingja could even be lent: Hjalti Skeggiason, about to set out on a dangerous voyage, asked Olaf II of Norway to lend him his. It usually appears in sleep in animal form, and can also be the spirit of a sleeping person in animal shape, like Bödvar Bjarki in the saga of Hrólfr Kraki.

long_description.id: Kata hamingja (Nordik Kuno, "keberuntungan") merujuk pada dua konsep: perwujudan untung baik seseorang atau keluarga, dan rupa yang berubah dari para pengubah wujud. Andy Orchard dan Rudolf Simek mencatat kemiripannya dengan fylgja. Dalam kepercayaan Nordik, ia juga dipahami sebagai kekuatan pelindung keluarga yang dapat digambarkan sebagai perempuan raksasa dan mengawasi perilaku keturunannya. Hamingja memberi kekayaan, keberhasilan, dan kekuasaan yang bertambah sepanjang hidup, dan kadang kata ini dipakai untuk kehormatan.
long_description.en: The word hamingja (Old Norse, 'luck') covers two ideas: the personified good fortune of a person or family, and the altered appearance of shape-shifters. Andy Orchard and Rudolf Simek note parallels with the fylgja. In Norse belief it was also understood as a family's guardian force, which could be pictured as a gigantic woman watching over the conduct of her descendants. The hamingja brings wealth, success and power that build up over a lifetime, and the word is sometimes used for honour.

role.en: Decides a person's luck and happiness.

short_description.id: Selma, atau Seljordsormen, adalah ular laut legendaris dalam cerita rakyat Norwegia yang konon hidup di Danau Seljord, Telemark.
short_description.en: Selma, or Seljordsormen, is a legendary sea serpent of Norwegian folklore said to live in Lake Seljord in Telemark.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Norwegia, Selma (Seljordsormen, "ular Seljord") adalah ular laut legendaris yang konon hidup di Danau Seljord sepanjang 13 kilometer di Kotamadya Seljord, Telemark. Makhluk ini sudah diperbincangkan sedikitnya sejak abad ke-18, dan kesaksian tentangnya cenderung memuncak pada musim panas yang panas dan tenang.
long_description.en: Norwegian folklore tells of Selma (Seljordsormen, 'the Seljord serpent'), a legendary serpent believed to dwell in the 13-kilometre Lake Seljord in Seljord Municipality, Telemark. short_description.id: Kucing troll adalah makhluk peliharaan penyihir dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia yang mencuri susu sapi dan krim untuk tuannya.
short_description.en: The troll cat is a witch's familiar of Scandinavian folklore that steals cows' milk and cream for its mistress.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia, kucing troll adalah makhluk peliharaan seorang penyihir. Ia mengisap susu sapi lalu memuntahkannya ke ember susu sang penyihir, dan masuk ke rumah-rumah untuk menjilat krim. Selain kucing, ada makhluk serupa seperti kelinci susu, terwelu susu, dan bola troll.
long_description.en: In Scandinavian folklore the troll cat is a witch's familiar. It sucked milk from cows and spat it into the witch's pails, and slipped into homes to lick up cream. Besides cats, similar creatures include the milk rabbit, the milk hare and the troll ball.

long_description.id: Penyihir konon membuatnya dari rambut manusia, kuku, serutan kayu, dan semacamnya. Nama Norwegia trollnøste dan trollnøa menunjukkan wujudnya seperti gulungan benang; jenis lain tampak seperti kucing biasa, dan melukainya akan melukai sang penyihir juga. Menembak kucing troll diyakini membuat susu menyembur dari lukanya, dan kucing itu harus dikubur bersama penyihirnya.
long_description.en: Witches were said to make it from human hair, nails, wood shavings and the like. The Norwegian names trollnøste and trollnøa show its shape, like a ball of yarn; another kind looked like an ordinary cat, and harming it harmed the witch too. Shooting a troll cat was believed to make milk spray from the wound, and it had to be buried with its witch.

long_description.id: Dalam kepercayaan Swedia, makhluk ini disebut bjära dan bisa berwujud terwelu, kucing, burung, atau gulungan benang; deskripsi tertua cara membuatnya berasal dari pengadilan sihir di Söderala, Hälsingland, tahun 1597. Kepercayaan ini tampaknya berkaitan dengan pengamatan benda yang dimuntahkan sapi, dan jamur lendir Fuligo septica dianggap kotoran kucing troll.
long_description.en: In Swedish belief the creature is called bjära and could take the form of a hare, cat, bird or ball of yarn; the oldest description of how to make one comes from a witch trial at Söderala, Hälsingland, in 1597. The belief seems linked to observing matter regurgitated by cattle, and the slime mould Fuligo septica was seen as troll-cat droppings.

short_description.id: Bahkauv adalah monster dalam cerita rakyat Aachen, Jerman, berupa anak sapi cacat bertaring yang mengintai di saluran air dan melompat ke pundak pemabuk di malam hari.
short_description.en: The Bahkauv is a monster of Aachen folklore in Germany, a deformed fanged calf that lurks in waterways and leaps onto drunkards' shoulders at night.

long_description.id: Bahkauv adalah monster mitos yang konon tinggal di Aachen, Jerman, dan dikenal dalam cerita rakyat Aachen dan Rheinland. Namanya berasal dari Bachkalb, "anak sapi sungai". Ia biasa digambarkan seperti anak sapi yang memanjang atau cacat dengan taring tajam, dan sering mengintai di dekat mata air, sungai kecil, dan selokan; saluran pembuangan dan mata air panas di bawah kota disebut sebagai tempat tinggalnya.
long_description.en: The Bahkauv is a mythical monster said to live in Aachen, Germany, and known in the folklore of Aachen and the Rhineland. Its name comes from Bachkalb, 'brook calf'. It is usually described as an elongated or deformed calf with sharp fangs that lurks near fountains, streams and sewers; the city's sewers and the hot springs beneath it are named as its home.

long_description.id: Menurut sage Aachen, ia tinggal di saluran air buangan mata air panas di Büchel, berwujud anak sapi besar berbulu kusut dengan gigi tajam, mata yang bersinar dalam gelap, cakar seperti beruang, ekor bersisik, dan rantai di leher serta kakinya. Pada malam hari ia menyerang orang mabuk dalam perjalanan pulang, melompat ke pundak mereka dan minta digendong sampai rumah; ia makin berat bila pembawanya berdoa dan makin ringan bila ia mengumpat.
long_description.en: In the Aachen legend it lived in the drain of the hot springs at the Büchel, shaped like a large shaggy calf with sharp teeth, eyes glowing in the dark, bear-like paws, a scaly tail and chains on its neck and legs. At night it attacked drunkards on their way home, jumping onto their shoulders to be carried home; it grew heavier when the bearer prayed and lighter when he cursed.

long_description.id: Meski begitu, Bahkauv tak pernah membunuh siapa pun dan tak pernah mengganggu perempuan atau anak-anak. Satu legenda menyebut Pippin Muda membunuh seekor Bahkauv yang berbaring di dekat mata air. Pada 1902 kota Aachen mendirikan patung Bahkauv di atas sumur tua yang dikaitkan dengannya; patung itu dilebur untuk logamnya pada Perang Dunia II, dan patung kedua dibangun pada 1967.
long_description.en: Even so, the Bahkauv never killed anyone and never troubled women or children. One legend says Pippin the Younger slew a Bahkauv lying by a spring. In 1902 Aachen erected a statue of the Bahkauv over an old well linked to it; the statue was melted down for its metal in World War II, and a second was built in 1967.

short_description.id: Hydrus adalah ular air dari bestiari abad pertengahan yang menyusup ke mulut buaya yang tidur lalu merobek perutnya dari dalam, lambang Kristus yang keluar dari neraka.
short_description.en: The hydrus is a water snake of medieval bestiaries that slips into a sleeping crocodile's mouth and tears its belly from inside, an emblem of Christ breaking out of Hell.

long_description.id: Hydrus, juga disebut Enhydros atau Ydrus, adalah makhluk bestiari Abad Pertengahan yang biasanya dianggap ular air, tetapi juga digambarkan sebagai burung, naga, atau luwak. Menurut Aberdeen Bestiary namanya berasal dari kata Yunani untuk air karena ia hidup di Sungai Nil. Plinius Tua menyebut bisanya paling kuat di antara ular, dengan hati sebagai penawarnya, dan Thomas dari Cantimpré menyebut gigitannya menimbulkan "penyakit boa".
long_description.en: The hydrus, also called Enhydros or Ydrus, is a creature of Medieval bestiaries usually taken as a water snake but also shown as a bird, dragon or mongoose. The Aberdeen Bestiary derives its name from the Greek for water because it lives in the Nile. Pliny the Elder called its venom the strongest of any snake, its liver the cure, and Thomas of Cantimpré said its bite causes the 'boa sickness'.

long_description.id: Hydrus membenci buaya: ia berlumur lumpur, menyelinap ke mulut buaya yang tidur, lalu merobek perutnya dari dalam. Tradisi Kristen menjadikannya lambang Kristus yang turun ke dunia orang mati dan bangkit, seperti dalam Bestiaire de Gervaise. Ia kadang dicampuradukkan dengan Hydra dari mitos Yunani.
long_description.en: The hydrus hates crocodiles: it coats itself in mud, slips into a sleeping crocodile's mouth and rips open its belly from inside. Christian tradition made it a symbol of Christ descending to the dead and rising, as in the Bestiaire de Gervaise. It is sometimes confused with the Hydra of Greek myth.

description.id: Bisanya lebih kuat dari ular mana pun; hatinya menjadi penawar.
description.en: Its venom is stronger than any snake's; its liver is the antidote.

note.en: Sometimes confused with it.

claims.quote: The Hydrus (also known as Enhydros, Enidros, Hildris, Hydra, Hidri, Idra, Idres, Ydre, Ydris, and Ydrus) is a creature from Medieval bestiaries.

statement.id: Hydrus (juga Enhydros, Enidros, Hildris, Hydra, Hidri, Idra, Idres, Ydre, Ydris, dan Ydrus) adalah makhluk dari bestiari Abad Pertengahan.
statement.en: The Hydrus (also Enhydros, Enidros, Hildris, Hydra, Hidri, Idra, Idres, Ydre, Ydris and Ydrus) is a creature of Medieval bestiaries.

claims.quote: A hydrus has no set appearance. Normally it is considered to be a water snake. Other animals the hydrus has been thought of as include a bird, a dragon, and a mongoose.

statement.id: Wujud hydrus tidak tetap; biasanya ia dianggap ular air, tetapi juga digambarkan sebagai burung, naga, atau luwak.
statement.en: The hydrus has no fixed look; it is usually taken to be a water snake, but also shown as a bird, a dragon or a mongoose.

claims.quote: Pliny the Elder described the hydrus as a amphibious serpent with stronger venom than any other snake. He also says that the hydrus' liver can be used as an antidote to its bite.

statement.id: Plinius Tua menggambarkan hydrus sebagai ular amfibi dengan bisa lebih kuat dari ular mana pun, dan hatinya dapat dipakai sebagai penawar gigitannya.
statement.en: Pliny the Elder described the hydrus as an amphibious serpent with venom stronger than any other snake's, whose liver can serve as an antidote to its bite.

claims.quote: They were said to be found in the Nile River. It is said that the hydrus hated crocodiles, and would intentionally roll in the mud and seek out a crocodile while it slept with its mouth open.

statement.id: Hydrus konon hidup di Sungai Nil dan membenci buaya; ia sengaja berguling di lumpur lalu mencari buaya yang tidur dengan mulut terbuka.
statement.en: They were said to live in the Nile and to hate crocodiles; the hydrus would roll in mud on purpose and seek out a crocodile sleeping with its mouth open.

claims.quote: Once inside the crocodile's stomach, the hydrus would burst free from the stomach lining, ripping out the crocodile's entrails and leaving it to die. In medieval Christian tradition, this bursting free from the crocodile became an emblem of the resurrection of Christ bursting free from Hell.

statement.id: Di dalam perut buaya, hydrus merobek dinding perut dan isi perut buaya itu hingga mati; dalam tradisi Kristen abad pertengahan, hal ini menjadi lambang kebangkitan Kristus yang keluar dari neraka.
statement.en: Inside the crocodile's stomach the hydrus tears free through the lining and entrails, leaving it to die; in medieval Christian tradition this became an emblem of Christ's resurrection breaking out of Hell.

claims.quote: Selon Thomas de Cantimpré, au XIIIe siècle, la morsure cause un effet de sidération, nommée la "maladie du boa".

statement.id: Menurut Thomas dari Cantimpré pada abad ke-13, gigitannya menimbulkan efek lumpuh yang disebut "penyakit boa".
statement.en: According to Thomas of Cantimpré in the 13th century, its bite causes a stunning effect called the 'boa sickness'.

claims.quote: Dans le Bestiaire de Gervaise, on retrouve la mention de ce récit, avec l'interprétation théologique du Christ descendu aux Enfers pour sauver les âmes.

statement.id: Bestiaire de Gervaise memuat kisah ini dengan tafsiran teologis tentang Kristus yang turun ke dunia orang mati untuk menyelamatkan jiwa-jiwa.
statement.en: The Bestiaire de Gervaise tells this story with the theological reading of Christ descending to Hell to save souls.

claims.quote: Certaines descriptions peuvent le mélanger avec d'autres serpents aquatiques ou avec l'hydre issue des mythes grecs.

statement.id: Sebagian gambaran mencampurkannya dengan ular air lain atau dengan Hydra dari mitos Yunani.
statement.en: Some descriptions mix it with other water snakes or with the Hydra of Greek myth.

claims.quote: За переказами з Абердинського бестіарію, ця істота живе в річці Нілі і називається гідром, позаяк живе в воді (гідро — з грец. «вода»).

statement.id: Menurut Aberdeen Bestiary, makhluk ini hidup di Sungai Nil dan dinamai hydrus karena hidup di air (hydro, bahasa Yunani "air").
statement.en: According to the Aberdeen Bestiary this creature lives in the Nile and is called hydrus because it lives in water (hydro, Greek 'water').

short_description.id: Iara adalah sosok perempuan air dalam mitologi Brasil yang berakar pada tradisi Tupi dan Guaraní, yang menyanyi di sungai dan memikat lelaki ke dasar air.
short_description.en: Iara is a water woman of Brazilian mythology rooted in Tupi and Guaraní tradition who sings in the rivers and lures men to the depths.

long_description.id: Iara adalah tokoh mitologi Brasil yang berakar pada mitologi Tupi dan Guaraní; namanya dari bahasa Nheengatu iiyara, "nyonya air". Ia sejenis siren yang tinggal di sungai atau danau dan menyanyikan lagu yang tak tertahankan pada malam hari, terutama di bawah sinar bulan. Suaranya memikat para lelaki, yang lalu mengikutinya ke kerajaannya di dasar air.
long_description.en: Iara is a figure of Brazilian mythology rooted in Tupi and Guaraní mythology; her name comes from Nheengatu iiyara, "lady of the water". She is a kind of siren who lives in rivers or lakes and sings irresistible songs at night, especially by moonlight. Her voice enchants men, who follow her to her realm at the bottom of the water.

long_description.id: Iara mungkin berkembang dari kisah Ipupiara, manusia ikan pemakan daging, lalu bercampur dengan mitos siren dan putri duyung Eropa. Sebagian penulis meyakini Iara versi asli berkulit gelap dan berambut hitam seperti penduduk asli, tetapi puisi Romantik abad ke-19 memberinya rambut pirang atau hijau dan mata biru atau hijau.
long_description.en: Iara may have grown from the lore of Ipupiara, a carnivorous fish-man, later blended with the European siren and mermaid. Some writers believe the original Iara was dark-skinned and black-haired like the indigenous people, but 19th-century Romantic poetry gave her blonde or green hair and blue or green eyes.

short_description.id: Ichneumon adalah hewan dalam sastra abad pertengahan, musuh naga yang melumuri diri dengan lumpur lalu menyerang naga, buaya, dan ular aspis.
short_description.en: The ichneumon is an animal of medieval literature, the dragon's enemy, which coats itself in mud and then attacks dragons, crocodiles and asps.

long_description.id: Ichneumon, dari bahasa Yunani "pelacak", adalah nama luwak Mesir yang dalam sastra abad pertengahan menjadi musuh naga. Ia melumuri diri dengan lumpur, menutup hidung dengan ekornya, lalu menyerang dan membunuh naga; ia juga melawan buaya dan ular aspis dengan cara sama. Bentuknya seperti musang ferret yang ramping, cepat, dan pandai melompat.
long_description.en: The ichneumon, Greek for 'tracker', was a name for the Egyptian mongoose that medieval literature turned into the dragon's enemy. It coats itself in mud, plugs its nose with its tail, and attacks and kills dragons; it fights crocodiles and asps the same way. It looks like a slim ferret, quick and a good jumper.

long_description.id: Plinius Tua menulis bahwa ia berlapis lumpur kering sebelum bertempur, dan Strabo menyebutnya masuk ke mulut buaya yang berjemur lalu keluar setelah memakan isi perutnya; penduduk Herakleopolis memujanya. Lewat penulis kuno ini, sastra Eropa membuatnya melawan basilisk dan cacatrix.
long_description.en: Pliny the Elder wrote that it armours itself in dried mud before battle, and Strabo that it enters a basking crocodile's mouth and comes out after eating its insides; the people of Heracleopolis worshipped it. Through these ancient writers, European literature set it against the basilisk and the cacatrix.

origin.id: Plinius Tua, Strabo, sastra abad pertengahan.
origin.en: Pliny the Elder, Strabo, medieval literature.

note.en: A dragon it fights.

claims.quote: In medieval literature, the ichneumon or echinemon was the enemy of the dragon. When it sees a dragon, the ichneumon covers itself with mud, and closing its nostrils with its tail, attacks and kills the dragon.

statement.id: Dalam sastra abad pertengahan, ichneumon atau echinemon adalah musuh naga: ketika melihat naga, ia melumuri diri dengan lumpur, menutup lubang hidungnya dengan ekor, lalu menyerang dan membunuh naga itu.
statement.en: In medieval literature the ichneumon or echinemon was the dragon's enemy: on seeing a dragon it coats itself in mud, closes its nostrils with its tail, and attacks and kills the dragon.

claims.quote: The ichneumon was also considered by some to be the enemy of the crocodile and the asp, and attacks them in the same way. The name was used for the pharaoh's rat, mongoose, or Egyptian mongoose (Herpestes ichneumon), which attacks snakes; it can also mean otter.

statement.id: Sebagian penulis juga menganggapnya musuh buaya dan ular aspis yang diserang dengan cara sama; nama ini dipakai untuk luwak Mesir (Herpestes ichneumon) yang menyerang ular, dan juga dapat berarti berang-berang.
statement.en: Some also thought it the enemy of the crocodile and the asp, attacking them the same way; the name was used for the Egyptian mongoose (Herpestes ichneumon), which attacks snakes, and can also mean otter.

claims.quote: Ichneumon (ἰχνεύμων) means "tracker" in Greek.

statement.id: Ichneumon (ἰχνεύμων) berarti "pelacak" dalam bahasa Yunani.
statement.en: Ichneumon (ἰχνεύμων) means 'tracker' in Greek.

claims.quote: It plunges itself repeatedly into the mud, and then dries itself in the sun: as soon as, by these means, it has armed itself with a sufficient number of coatings, it proceeds to the combat.

statement.id: Menurut Plinius Tua, ia berulang kali mencelupkan diri ke lumpur lalu mengeringkannya di bawah matahari, dan setelah berlapis cukup tebal ia maju bertempur.
statement.en: According to Pliny the Elder it plunges repeatedly into mud and dries in the sun, and once armed with enough coatings it goes into battle.

claims.quote: They lie in wait for the crocodiles, when the latter are basking in the sun with their mouths open; they then drop into their jaws, and eating through their intestines and belly, issue out of the dead body.

statement.id: Menurut Strabo, ichneumon menunggu buaya yang berjemur dengan mulut terbuka, masuk ke rahangnya, lalu memakan usus dan perutnya hingga keluar dari bangkainya.
statement.en: According to Strabo, ichneumons wait for crocodiles basking with open mouths, drop into their jaws, and eat through the guts and belly to come out of the dead body.

claims.quote: but the Heracleotæ worship the ichneumon, which is most destructive both to crocodiles and asps.

statement.id: Strabo mencatat penduduk Herakleopolis memuja ichneumon, pembasmi buaya dan ular aspis.
statement.en: Strabo records that the people of Heracleopolis worship the ichneumon, the great destroyer of crocodiles and asps.

claims.quote: The ichneumon is shaped similarly to a ferret, although much slimmer in its shape, and the head is elongated. Also, it is an animal that can move swiftly and is able to jump a couple of yards with a single leap.

statement.id: Bentuknya mirip musang ferret tetapi jauh lebih ramping dengan kepala memanjang, bergerak cepat dan dapat melompat beberapa meter sekali loncat.
statement.en: It is shaped like a ferret but much slimmer, with an elongated head, moves swiftly and can leap a couple of yards in one bound.

claims.quote: Par l’intermédiaire des chroniqueurs antiques, notamment Pline l’Ancien, il sera ponctuellement associé à d’autres animaux dans la littérature médiévale européenne où il affrontera des dragons comme le basilic ou la cacatrix.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Prancis, lewat penulis kuno seperti Plinius Tua, dalam sastra Eropa abad pertengahan ia dikaitkan dengan hewan lain dan melawan naga seperti basilisk atau cacatrix.
statement.en: According to the French article, through ancient writers such as Pliny the Elder it was linked in medieval European literature with other animals and fought dragons such as the basilisk or the cacatrix.

claims.quote: L’animal était utilisé par les Égyptiens et les indiens dans les périodes anciennes pour se débarrasser des serpents venimeux, comme le cobra, ou encore d’autres reptiles comme les crocodiles.

statement.id: Hewan ini dipakai orang Mesir dan India pada masa kuno untuk menyingkirkan ular berbisa seperti kobra dan reptil lain seperti buaya.
statement.en: The animal was used by Egyptians and Indians in ancient times to get rid of venomous snakes such as the cobra and other reptiles such as crocodiles.

claims.quote: En la literatura medieval, l'ichneumon o echinemon era l'enemic del drac.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Katalan juga menyebut ichneumon atau echinemon musuh naga dalam sastra abad pertengahan.
statement.en: The Catalan article likewise calls the ichneumon or echinemon the enemy of the dragon in medieval literature.
