short_description.id: Luisón adalah manusia serigala mitologi Guarani, putra ketujuh Tau dan Kerana, dan menurut kepercayaan Paraguay serta Argentina anak laki-laki ketujuh dalam keluarga akan menjadi Luisón.
short_description.en: The Luisón is the werewolf of Guarani mythology, seventh son of Tau and Kerana, and by belief in Paraguay and Argentina a family's seventh son will become one.

long_description.id: Luisón atau Lobizón adalah satu dari tujuh binatang legendaris Paraguay, putra ketujuh Tau dan Kerana yang menanggung kutukan terberat. Ia anjing raksasa yang mengerikan dan berada di persimpangan kehidupan dan kematian; versi Portugis menggambarkannya mirip serigala atau monyet bermata merah. Anak laki-laki ketujuh dipercaya berubah menjadi Luisón pada ulang tahun ke-13 atau pada malam bulan purnama hari Jumat dan Selasa.
long_description.en: Counted among Paraguay's seven legendary beasts, the Luisón or Lobizón is the seventh son of Tau and Kerana and bears the heaviest curse. He is a hideous giant dog standing at the crossroads of life and death; the Portuguese version likens him to a wolf or red-eyed monkey. A seventh son is believed to turn into a Luisón on his 13th birthday or on full-moon Friday and Tuesday nights.

long_description.id: Mitos ini mungkin berpadu dengan cerita manusia serigala yang dibawa pendatang lewat serigala surai. Karena dulu ada orang yang mengorbankan anak ketujuh, sejak abad ke-19 Presiden Argentina menjadi wali baptis anak laki-laki ketujuh, kebiasaan yang diresmikan Juan Domingo Perón pada 1973.
long_description.en: The myth may have merged with the werewolf lore settlers brought, through the maned wolf. Because some people once sacrificed their seventh sons, since the 19th century the President of Argentina has stood godparent to seventh sons, a custom made law by Juan Domingo Perón in 1973.

role.en: The curse of the seventh son.

description.id: Perón meresmikan perwalian presiden atas anak ketujuh.
description.en: Perón makes presidential godparenthood of seventh sons law.

claims.quote: The Luison (Paraguayan Guaraní: Luisõ; Spanish: Luisón or Lobizón) is one of the seven legendary beasts of Paraguay, and is the seventh and last son of Tau and Kerana. The myth is known also in Argentina and says that in a family with seven male children, the last child will become Luisón.

statement.id: Luisón (Guarani Paraguay: Luisõ; Spanyol: Luisón atau Lobizón) adalah satu dari tujuh binatang legendaris Paraguay, putra ketujuh dan terakhir Tau dan Kerana; mitos ini juga dikenal di Argentina dan menyebut bahwa dalam keluarga dengan tujuh anak laki-laki, anak terakhir akan menjadi Luisón.
statement.en: The Luisón (Paraguayan Guarani Luisõ; Spanish Luisón or Lobizón) is one of the seven legendary beasts of Paraguay, the seventh and last son of Tau and Kerana; the myth is also known in Argentina and holds that in a family of seven sons the last will become a Luisón.

claims.quote: In the original version of the myth, Luisón was the seventh and last child of Tau and Kerana, and thus was the most accursed. He appeared to be a giant dog, and was said to be extremely ugly, even horrendous looking.

statement.id: Dalam versi asli, sebagai anak ketujuh Tau dan Kerana ia paling terkutuk, tampak seperti anjing raksasa yang sangat buruk rupa.
statement.en: In the original myth, as the seventh child of Tau and Kerana he was the most accursed, looking like a giant, hideous dog.

claims.quote: The myth tells that the seventh son in a family will transform on his 13th birthday.

statement.id: Mitos menyebut anak laki-laki ketujuh dalam keluarga akan berubah pada ulang tahunnya yang ke-13.
statement.en: The myth says a family's seventh son will transform on his 13th birthday.

claims.quote: The maned wolf, a slender, wolf-like, stilted canid that moves with shambling steps, fitted the popular depiction of the werewolf and ultimately it was syncretized with local guarani myths.

statement.id: Serigala surai, anjing liar ramping berkaki panjang yang berjalan terseok, cocok dengan gambaran manusia serigala yang dibawa pendatang dan akhirnya berpadu dengan mitos Guarani setempat.
statement.en: The maned wolf, a slender long-legged wolf-like canid with a shambling gait, fitted the werewolf image brought by settlers and was eventually blended with local Guarani myths.

claims.quote: It has been customary since the 19th century for the President of Argentina to be named the "godparent" of each seventh male child of a married couple. This custom arose because superstitious people sometimes sacrificed their seventh son out of fear of the "possibility" that a Luisón had been born.

statement.id: Sejak abad ke-19 Presiden Argentina biasa menjadi wali baptis setiap anak laki-laki ketujuh, kebiasaan yang muncul karena orang yang percaya takhayul kadang mengorbankan anak ketujuh mereka karena takut ia Luisón.
statement.en: Since the 19th century the President of Argentina has customarily been godparent to every seventh son, a custom born because superstitious people sometimes sacrificed their seventh son for fear he was a Luisón.

claims.quote: On 12 March 1973, President Juan Domingo Perón gave legal form to this custom through Decree No. 848, known as the presidential sponsorship law.

statement.id: Pada 12 Maret 1973 Presiden Juan Domingo Perón meresmikan kebiasaan ini lewat Dekret No. 848, yang dikenal sebagai undang-undang perwalian presiden.
statement.en: On 12 March 1973 President Juan Domingo Perón made the custom law through Decree No. 848, the presidential sponsorship law.

short_description.id: Naga dalam puisi Inggris Kuno Beowulf adalah lawan ketiga dan terakhir sang pahlawan: penimbun harta penyembur api yang mengamuk karena sebuah piala dicuri dari sarangnya.
short_description.en: The dragon of the Old English poem Beowulf is the hero's third and last foe: a fire-breathing treasure-keeper that rampages after a cup is stolen from its lair.

long_description.id: Babak akhir puisi Anglo-Saxon Beowulf memuat pertarungan Beowulf dengan seekor naga, monster ketiga yang dihadapinya. Setelah memerintah kaum Geat dengan bijak selama lima puluh tahun, seorang budak membangunkan dan membuat naga itu murka dengan mencuri piala berhias permata dari sarangnya. Naga itu lalu membakar rumah-rumah dan tanah kaum Geat, termasuk rumah Beowulf, sehingga sang raja memutuskan melawannya sendiri.
long_description.en: The final act of the Anglo-Saxon poem Beowulf has Beowulf fighting a dragon, the third monster he faces. After he has ruled the Geats wisely for fifty years, a slave wakes and enrages the dragon by stealing a jewelled cup from its lair. The dragon then burns the Geats' homes and lands, Beowulf's included, and the king resolves to fight it himself.

long_description.id: Para pengiringnya lari ketakutan, kecuali Wiglaf yang tetap bertarung di sisinya. Ketika naga itu melukai Beowulf secara fatal, Wiglaf menyerangnya dengan pedang, dan Beowulf membunuhnya dengan belatinya. Naga itu konon telah tidur di atas harta selama tiga ratus tahun; ia digambarkan bisa terbang dan merayap, menyembur api, dan gigitannya berbisa.
long_description.en: His thanes flee in terror, except Wiglaf, who fights at his side. When the dragon wounds Beowulf mortally, Wiglaf strikes it with his sword and Beowulf kills it with his dagger. The dragon is said to have slept on the treasure for three hundred years; it is described as able to fly and crawl, breathing fire, with a venomous bite.

long_description.id: Beowulf adalah karya sastra Inggris pertama yang menampilkan pembunuh naga, dan penyairnya yang pertama memadukan berbagai motif Jermanik menjadi naga penyembur api yang khas. Pertarungan ini melambangkan perlawanan Beowulf terhadap kejahatan dan kehancuran, sedangkan naga itu bertindak sebagai "raja emas" tiruan yang membalas pencurian satu piala dengan menyerang seluruh kerajaan. Naga Beowulf diadaptasi J. R. R. Tolkien untuk Dunia Tengah dalam The Hobbit (1937).
long_description.en: Beowulf is the first work of English literature to present a dragonslayer, and its poet was the first to combine Germanic motifs into a distinctive fire-breathing dragon. The fight symbolises Beowulf's stand against evil and destruction, while the dragon acts as a mock 'goldking', avenging the theft of one cup by attacking the whole kingdom. J. R. R. Tolkien later reworked this dragon for his Middle-earth novel The Hobbit (1937).

famous_for.en: Killing Beowulf and dying with him.

did_you_know.id: Naga Beowulf disebut salah satu contoh paling awal naga Eropa dalam sastra.
did_you_know.en: The Beowulf dragon is called one of the earliest examples of the European dragon in literature.

summary.en: A slave steals a cup from the dragon's hoard; the dragon burns the Geats' land, and Beowulf with Wiglaf kills it, but Beowulf is mortally wounded and dies.

statement.en: Beowulf rules wisely for fifty years until a slave wakes and angers a dragon by stealing a jewelled cup from its lair; the dragon burns the Geats' homes and lands, Beowulf resolves to fight it himself, and when it wounds him fatally, Wiglaf strikes with his sword and Beowulf kills it with his dagger.

claims.quote: Beowulf is the first piece of English literature to present a dragonslayer. Although the Beowulf dragon exhibits many existing motifs common to Germanic tradition, the Beowulf poet was the first to combine features and present a distinctive fire-breathing dragon. The Beowulf dragon was adapted for Middle-earth in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Hobbit (1937)

statement.id: Beowulf adalah karya sastra Inggris pertama yang menampilkan pembunuh naga; walau naganya memuat banyak motif umum tradisi Jermanik, penyair Beowulf yang pertama memadukannya menjadi naga penyembur api yang khas, dan naga ini diadaptasi untuk Dunia Tengah dalam The Hobbit (1937) karya J. R. R. Tolkien.
statement.en: Beowulf is the first English work to present a dragonslayer; though its dragon shows many common Germanic motifs, the poet was the first to combine them into a distinctive fire-breathing dragon, which was adapted for Middle-earth in J. R. R. Tolkien's The Hobbit (1937).

claims.quote: The legend of the dragonslayer already existed in Norse sagas such as the tale of Sigurd and Fáfnir, and the Beowulf poet incorporates motifs and themes common to dragonlore in the poem.

statement.id: Legenda pembunuh naga sudah ada dalam saga Nordik seperti kisah Sigurd dan Fáfnir, dan penyair Beowulf memasukkan motif serta tema umum kisah naga ke dalam puisinya.
statement.en: The dragonslayer legend already existed in Norse sagas such as the tale of Sigurd and Fáfnir, and the Beowulf poet incorporates common dragonlore motifs.

claims.quote: The fight with the dragon symbolizes Beowulf's stand against evil and destruction, and, as the hero, he knows that failure will bring destruction to his people after many years of peace. The dragon itself acts as a mock "goldking"; one who sees attacking Beowulf's kingdom as suitable retribution for the theft of just a single cup.

statement.id: Pertarungan dengan naga melambangkan perlawanan Beowulf terhadap kejahatan dan kehancuran; naga itu sendiri bertindak sebagai "raja emas" tiruan yang menganggap serangan terhadap kerajaan Beowulf sebagai balasan pantas atas pencurian satu piala.
statement.en: The fight symbolises Beowulf's stand against evil and destruction; the dragon acts as a mock 'goldking', treating an attack on Beowulf's kingdom as fit retribution for the theft of a single cup.

claims.quote: Un dragon (draca ou wyrm en vieil anglais) est le troisième et dernier adversaire du héros Beowulf dans le poème épique anglo-saxon Beowulf. statement.en: The dragon (Old English draca or wyrm) is the third and last foe of Beowulf in the Anglo-Saxon epic, one of the earliest European literary dragons: an evil reptile able to fly and crawl, breathing fire, with a poisonous bite.

statement.en: The theft enraged the dragon, which had slept on the treasure for three hundred years, and it left its lair to wreak destruction on the Geats' kingdom in revenge.

short_description.id: Drude adalah roh malam perempuan yang jahat dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, sejenis Alp atau nenek sihir yang duduk di dada orang tidur dan menimbulkan mimpi buruk, terutama di Jerman selatan.
short_description.en: The drude is a malevolent female night spirit of German folklore, a kind of Alp or witch-hag that sits on sleepers' chests and causes nightmares, especially in southern Germany.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, drude, juga trude, adalah roh malam perempuan yang jahat, sejenis Alp atau nenek sihir yang dikaitkan dengan mimpi buruk dan terutama dikenal di Jerman selatan. Ia duduk di dada orang yang tidur dan menimbulkan mimpi buruk, rasa tertekan, dan sesak napas; dalam tradisi Bayern kemudian, ada pula pasangan lelakinya yang disebut Truder atau Truderer.
long_description.en: In German folklore the drude, also trude, is a malevolent female night spirit, a kind of Alp or witch-hag linked with nightmares and known especially in southern Germany. She sits on sleepers' chests causing nightmares, oppression and breathlessness; later Bavarian tradition also gave her male counterparts called Truder or Truderer.

long_description.id: Kata ini tercatat sebagai trute dalam bahasa Jerman Hulu Pertengahan akhir dan paling mungkin berkaitan dengan kata Nordik Kuno troða, "menginjak, menginjak-injak"; pada abad ke-16 trute juga dipakai sebagai sebutan umum untuk penyihir. Menurut sebagian cerita, drude adalah penyihir yang dapat mengubah ukurannya, masuk rumah sebagai makhluk mungil atau menjadi raksasa, dan hanya rohnya yang keluar dari tubuh untuk menyiksa orang tidur.
long_description.en: The word is attested as trute in late Middle High German and most plausibly relates to Old Norse troða, 'to tread, trample'; in the 16th century trute was also a general word for 'witch'. In some lore the drude is a witch able to change size, entering houses as a tiny being or growing into a giantess, and only her spirit leaves the body to torment sleepers.

long_description.id: Di Jerman selatan dan Austria, drude adalah perempuan yang dikutuk mencari korban setiap malam, manusia, hewan, bahkan pohon dan batu; rohnya masuk lewat celah dan lubang kunci dalam rupa kucing, sedotan, atau bulu. Penangkalnya antara lain tanda Drudenfuß, yang konon berasal dari jejak kakinya yang mirip kaki burung, serta Drudenstein, batu kerikil berlubang yang digantung di loteng.
long_description.en: In southern Germany and Austria the drude is a woman condemned to seek a victim every night, people, animals, even trees and stones; her soul enters through cracks and keyholes in the form of a cat, a straw or a feather. Protections include the Drudenfuß sign, said to come from her bird-like footprint, and the Drudenstein, a holed pebble hung in the roof.

claims.quote: The word is attested as trute in late Middle High German. ... The word trute also came to be used as a generic term for "witch" in the 16th century (Hans Sachs).

statement.en: The word is attested as trute in late Middle High German, and in the 16th century trute also became a general term for 'witch'.

claims.quote: Middle High German trute is etymologically related to Old Norse troða ("to tread, to trample"), i.e., is related to modern German verb treten ("to tread, to step"); this is considered the most plausible etymology in modern philological opinion. ... In later Bavarian folklore tradition, the female Trude had male counterparts called Truder , Trudner , or Truderer

statement.id: Kata Jerman Hulu Pertengahan trute berkaitan dengan Nordik Kuno troða ("menginjak, menginjak-injak") dan kata Jerman modern treten, etimologi yang dianggap paling masuk akal; dalam tradisi Bayern kemudian, Trude perempuan punya pasangan lelaki bernama Truder, Trudner, atau Truderer.
statement.en: Middle High German trute relates to Old Norse troða ('to tread, trample') and German treten, the etymology deemed most plausible; in later Bavarian tradition the female Trude had male counterparts called Truder, Trudner or Truderer.

claims.quote: Drude is held responsible for causing the nightmare Alpdruck ("elf pressure"), thus considered just a subtype of an Alp, as far as its attack behavior is concerned. According to some folklore, the drude is a witch who can assume various sizes, small or large ... It is also said that only the witch's spirit drifts out of body to perform their handiwork tormenting people (in their sleep).

statement.id: Drude dianggap penyebab mimpi buruk Alpdruck ("tekanan elf") sehingga dalam cara menyerang dipandang subtipe Alp; menurut sebagian cerita ia penyihir yang bisa berukuran kecil atau besar, dan konon hanya rohnya yang keluar dari tubuh untuk menyiksa orang yang tidur.
statement.en: The drude is blamed for the Alpdruck nightmare ('elf pressure') and so counted a subtype of the Alp in attack; in some lore she is a witch who can be small or large, and only her spirit leaves the body to torment sleepers.

claims.quote: Eine Drude (auch Drute, Trude, Trute, Trut, männlich Drud, Druder, Drudner, Trutner oder bairisch Truderer) ist ein Wesen des Volksglaubens, das sich nachts auf die Brust von Schlafenden setzt und Albträume, Beklemmungen und Atemnot verursacht. ... sowie im oldenburgischen Raum Walrider, Walriderske.

statement.id: Drude (juga Drute, Trude, Trute; lelaki Druder atau dalam bahasa Bayern Truderer) adalah makhluk kepercayaan rakyat yang pada malam hari duduk di dada orang tidur dan menimbulkan mimpi buruk, rasa tertekan, dan sesak napas; di Oldenburg ia disebut Walrider atau Walriderske.
statement.en: The Drude (also Drute, Trude, Trute; male Druder or Bavarian Truderer) is a folk-belief being that sits on sleepers' chests at night causing nightmares, oppression and breathlessness; in the Oldenburg area it is called Walrider or Walriderske.

claims.quote: Hier sind Frauen, die dazu verdammt sind, sich jede Nacht ein Opfer zum Drücken suchen zu müssen: Erwachsene, Kinder und Haustiere werden heimgesucht, aber auch Bäume und Steine. ... kann als Geist durch kleinste Spalten und Schlüssellöcher in ein Zimmer dringen und dann in verschiedener Gestalt erscheinen (z. B. als Katze, Strohhalm oder Feder).

statement.id: Di Jerman selatan dan Austria, drude adalah perempuan yang dikutuk mencari korban setiap malam, orang dewasa, anak, hewan, juga pohon dan batu; rohnya masuk lewat celah dan lubang kunci dan tampil dalam berbagai rupa seperti kucing, sedotan, atau bulu.
statement.en: As drudes these pressing spirits are widespread in southern Germany and Austria: women condemned to find a victim each night, adults, children, animals, even trees and stones; their soul leaves the body, slips through cracks and keyholes and appears as a cat, straw or feather.

claims.quote: Das Zauberzeichen Drudenfuß, auch Drudenkreuz genannt, soll gegen sie schützen. Der Ursprung dieses Zeichens liegt der Sage nach im vogelartigen Fußabdruck einer Drude.

statement.id: Tanda gaib Drudenfuß, juga disebut Drudenkreuz, konon melindungi dari drude; menurut sage, tanda ini berasal dari jejak kaki drude yang mirip kaki burung.
statement.en: The magic sign Drudenfuß, also Drudenkreuz, is said to protect against them; by legend it comes from a drude's bird-like footprint.

claims.quote: Ebenfalls abwehrende Wirkung sollten Drudensteine (auch Hühnergott genannt) haben, die Kieselsteine mit einem natürlichen Loch, dem sogenannten Auge sind. Diese wurden zur Abwehr mit einem Band oder einer Schnur im Dachstuhl des Hauses aufgehängt.

statement.id: Drudenstein (juga Hühnergott), kerikil dengan lubang alami yang disebut "mata", juga dipercaya menangkal drude dan digantung dengan tali di rangka atap rumah.
statement.en: Drudensteine (also Hühnergott), pebbles with a natural hole called the 'eye', were also believed to ward drudes off and were hung by a cord in the roof.

short_description.id: Ekke Nekkepenn adalah tokoh legenda Frisia Utara, digambarkan sebagai lelaki laut yang tinggal bersama istrinya Rahn di dasar Laut Utara dan mengusili para pelaut serta penduduk pulau.
short_description.en: Ekke Nekkepenn is a figure of North Frisian legend, pictured as a sea-dwelling man who shares the North Sea floor with his wife Rahn and teases sailors and islanders.

long_description.id: Ekke Nekkepenn (juga Eke Nekepen dan ejaan lain) adalah tokoh legenda Frisia Utara. Pada pertengahan abad ke-19, peneliti lokal, ahli folklor, dan seniman grafis Christian Peter Hansen menggambarkannya sebagai lelaki laut yang tinggal bersama istrinya Rahn di dasar Laut Utara dan mengusili para pelaut serta penduduk kepulauan Frisia Utara. Dalam satu uraian ia disebut padanan Ægir dalam banyak hal.
long_description.en: Ekke Nekkepenn (also Eke Nekepen and other spellings) is a figure of North Frisian legend. Christian Peter Hansen, a Sylt folklorist, local historian and printmaker of the mid-1800s, cast him as a merman sharing the North Sea floor with his wife Rahn and teasing sailors and the people of the North Frisian Islands. One account calls him a counterpart of Ægir in many respects.

long_description.id: Dalam kisah Hansen, Ekke Nekkepenn meminta istri seorang kapten Sylt, yang kapalnya diterjang badai dalam perjalanan ke Inggris, membantu persalinan anaknya; setelah berhasil, perempuan itu kembali ke permukaan dengan hadiah emas dan perak. Bertahun-tahun kemudian, karena Rahn telah "tua dan keriput", ia ingin menjadikan istri kapten itu istrinya dan menyuruh Rahn menggiling garam di dasar laut hingga pusarannya menenggelamkan kapal Sylt.
long_description.en: In Hansen's tale Ekke Nekkepenn asks the wife of a Sylt captain, whose England-bound ship is caught in a storm, to help with his child's birth; afterwards she returns to the surface with gifts of gold and silver. Years later, since Rahn has grown 'old and wrinkly', he wants the captain's wife for himself and has Rahn grind salt on the seabed until the whirlpool drags the Sylt ship down.

long_description.id: Dalam versi lain, ia jatuh cinta kepada gadis dari Rantum yang dipaksa menerimanya, lalu berjanji membebaskannya bila ia bisa menyebut nama lengkapnya; gadis itu akhirnya mendengar nyanyian dari bukit pasir yang menyebut nama Ekke Nekkepenn. Theodor Storm memasukkan sosok peri api bernama Eckeneckepenn yang membuat ladang layu dalam kisahnya Die Regentrude.
long_description.en: In another version he falls in love with a girl from Rantum who is forced to accept him, then promises her freedom if she can name him in full; she finally overhears a song from the dunes revealing the name Ekke Nekkepenn. Theodor Storm put a little fire-man called Eckeneckepenn, who withers the fields, into his tale Die Regentrude.

who.en: A merman of the North Sea.

role.en: Plays tricks on seafarers and islanders.

famous_for.en: The song that reveals his secret name.

did_you_know.id: Dalam satu legenda, gadis dari Rantum terbebas dari Ekke Nekkepenn setelah mendengar nyanyiannya sendiri yang menyebut namanya dari balik bukit pasir.
did_you_know.en: In one legend a girl from Rantum is freed from Ekke Nekkepenn after overhearing his own song from the dunes that revealed his name.

summary.id: Ia meminta bantuan istri kapten untuk persalinan istrinya Rahn, lalu bertahun-tahun kemudian menenggelamkan kapal Sylt untuk mengambil perempuan itu.
summary.en: He seeks the captain's wife's help for Rahn's childbirth, then years later sinks the Sylt ship to take her.

note.id: Istri Ekke Nekkepenn di dasar Laut Utara.
note.en: Ekke Nekkepenn's wife on the North Sea floor.

note.id: Dalam satu uraian ia padanan Ægir.
note.en: In one account his counterpart is Ægir.

claims.quote: is a North Frisian legendary figure. In the middle of the 19th century, the local researcher, folklorist, and graphic artist Christian Peter Hansen ... portrayed Ekke Nekkepenn as a merman who lives with his wife Rahn at the bottom of the North Sea and plays mischievous tricks on seafarers and residents of the North Frisian Islands.

statement.id: Ekke Nekkepenn (juga Eke Nekepen) adalah tokoh legenda Frisia Utara; pada pertengahan abad ke-19 peneliti lokal, ahli folklor, dan seniman grafis Christian Peter Hansen menggambarkannya sebagai lelaki laut yang tinggal bersama istrinya Rahn di dasar Laut Utara dan mengusili pelaut serta penduduk kepulauan Frisia Utara.
statement.en: Ekke Nekkepenn (also Eke Nekepen) is a North Frisian legendary figure; in the mid-19th century the local researcher, folklorist and artist Christian Peter Hansen portrayed him as a merman living with his wife Rahn on the North Sea floor and playing tricks on seafarers and North Frisian islanders.

claims.quote: In Theodor Storms 1866 veröffentlichter Novelle Die Regentrude taucht ein Feuermännlein mit dem Namen Eckeneckepenn auf, das mit seinem Schadenzauber für das Verdorren der Felder sorgt.

statement.id: Dalam novel Theodor Storm Die Regentrude yang terbit 1866, muncul peri api kecil bernama Eckeneckepenn yang dengan sihir jahatnya membuat ladang layu.
statement.en: In Theodor Storm's novella Die Regentrude, published in 1866, a little fire-man called Eckeneckepenn appears who withers the fields with harmful magic.

claims.quote: Die Erzählung beginnt damit, dass Ekke Nekkepenn die Frau des Kapitäns eines im Sturm nach England laufenden Sylter Schiffes um Hilfe bei der Geburt seines Kindes bittet. Die schöne und hilfsbereite Kapitänsfrau wird vom Meermann zu seiner auf dem Grunde der Nordsee lebenden Frau Rahn geführt und kommt nach gelungener Geburt reichbeschenkt mit Gold und Silber an die Meeresoberfläche zurück.

statement.id: Kisahnya bermula ketika Ekke Nekkepenn meminta istri kapten kapal Sylt yang diterjang badai menuju Inggris membantu persalinan anaknya; perempuan itu dibawa ke istrinya Rahn di dasar Laut Utara dan, setelah persalinan berhasil, kembali ke permukaan dengan hadiah emas dan perak.
statement.en: The tale begins with Ekke Nekkepenn asking the wife of the captain of a storm-tossed Sylt ship bound for England to help with his child's birth; she is led to his wife Rahn on the North Sea floor and, after a successful birth, returns to the surface richly gifted with gold and silver.

claims.quote: Several years later, Ekke Nekkepenn remembered this incident and decides – now that Rahn has become "old and wrinkly" – to take the captain's wife as his own. When he sees the Rantumer Captain's ship one day, he persuades Rahn, who's sitting on the seabed, to grind salt, and the resulting powerful vortex pulls down the Sylt ship

statement.id: Bertahun-tahun kemudian, karena Rahn telah "tua dan keriput", Ekke Nekkepenn ingin mengambil istri kapten itu; saat melihat kapal kapten dari Rantum, ia membujuk Rahn yang duduk di dasar laut untuk menggiling garam, dan pusaran kuat yang timbul menenggelamkan kapal Sylt itu.
statement.en: Years later, with Rahn now 'old and wrinkly', Ekke Nekkepenn decides to take the captain's wife; seeing the Rantum captain's ship, he gets Rahn on the seabed to grind salt, and the strong vortex pulls the Sylt ship down.

claims.quote: Ekke blev forelsket i en ung pige fra Rantum, som blev tvunget til at give ham jaordet. Senere fortrød hun sit ja. Ekke lovede hende omsider, at hvis hun indenfor den næste aften kunne nævne ham ved hans fulde navn, så skulle hun få sin frihed igen. Men ingen kendte navnet, indtil hun ved stranden hørte en sang, der lød ud fra klitterne:

statement.id: Ekke jatuh cinta kepada gadis muda dari Rantum yang dipaksa menerimanya; ketika gadis itu menyesal, Ekke berjanji membebaskannya bila sebelum malam berikutnya ia dapat menyebut nama lengkapnya, dan tak seorang pun tahu nama itu sampai ia mendengar nyanyian dari bukit pasir di pantai.
statement.en: Ekke fell in love with a young girl from Rantum who was forced to say yes; when she regretted it, he promised her freedom if by the next evening she could name him in full, and no one knew the name until she heard a song from the dunes by the beach.

claims.quote: Ekke Nekkepenn (på førfrisisk Eke Nekepen) er en nordfrisisk sagnfigur. Ifølge sagnet lever figuren sammen med sin kone Ran på bunden af Vesterhavet og driller søfarere og beboerne på de nordfrisiske øer. Han modsvarer på mange punkter Ægir. ... Stoffet blev også indarbejdet i Theodor Storms novelle Die Regentrude fra 1863.

statement.id: Ekke Nekkepenn (Frisia Föhr: Eke Nekepen) adalah tokoh legenda Frisia Utara yang menurut sage tinggal bersama istrinya Ran di dasar Laut Utara dan mengusili pelaut serta penduduk pulau; dalam banyak hal ia padanan Ægir, dan kisahnya juga diolah dalam novel Theodor Storm Die Regentrude dari 1863.
statement.en: Ekke Nekkepenn (Föhr Frisian Eke Nekepen) is a North Frisian legendary figure who by legend lives with his wife Ran on the North Sea floor teasing seafarers and islanders; he corresponds in many ways to Ægir, and the material was also worked into Theodor Storm's novella Die Regentrude of 1863.

short_description.id: Lusca adalah monster laut dalam cerita rakyat Karibia yang konon hidup di blue hole dekat Pulau Andros, Bahama, dan digambarkan sebagai gurita atau sotong raksasa.
short_description.en: The Lusca is a sea monster of Caribbean folklore said to live in the blue holes near Andros, Bahamas, described as a giant octopus or cuttlefish.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Karibia, Lusca adalah monster laut yang konon hidup di blue hole dekat Andros, Bahama. Ia digambarkan sebagai gurita raksasa, sotong raksasa, atau setengah hiu setengah gurita; namanya penggalan dari Mollusca.
long_description.en: In Caribbean folklore the Lusca is a sea monster said to live in the blue holes near Andros in the Bahamas. It is described as a giant octopus, a giant cuttlefish or half shark, half octopus; its name is a clipped form of Mollusca.

long_description.id: Pada 1872 J. S. George dari Nassau melaporkan gurita raksasa yang ditemukan mati di pantai. Kemudian pemandu setempat bercerita kepada ahli biologi laut Bruce S. Wright tentang lusca setengah gurita setengah naga yang tinggal di gua kapur bawah danau. Monster St. Augustine yang terdampar di Florida pada 1896 dianggap salah satu kandidat spesimen lusca.
long_description.en: In 1872 J. S. George of Nassau reported a colossal octopus found dead on the beach. Later a local guide told marine biologist Bruce S. Wright of a half-octopus, half-dragon lusca living in limestone caves under a lake. The St. Augustine monster stranded in Florida in 1896 is considered a candidate lusca specimen.

statement.en: In Caribbean folklore the Lusca is a sea monster said to live around the blue holes near Andros, an island in the Bahamas.

claims.quote: The first reported sighting of something resembling the traditional description of the Lusca in the area was in 1872, when J. S. George of Nassau in the Bahamas wrote to the American Naturalist describing a "colossal octopus" found dead on the beach.

statement.id: Laporan pertama yang mirip gambaran Lusca muncul pada 1872, ketika J. S. George dari Nassau menulis ke American Naturalist tentang "gurita raksasa" yang ditemukan mati di pantai.
statement.en: The first report resembling the Lusca came in 1872, when J. S. George of Nassau wrote to the American Naturalist about a "colossal octopus" found dead on the beach.

claims.quote: marine biologist Bruce S. Wright was told by a local guide that some limestone caverns beneath a lake were home to a monster called the lusca, described as a large, half-octopus, half-dragon animal, with powerful, sucker-tipped tentacles, which lived in banana holes and blue holes.

statement.id: Ahli biologi laut Bruce S. Wright mendengar dari pemandu setempat bahwa gua kapur di bawah sebuah danau dihuni lusca, makhluk besar setengah gurita setengah naga dengan tentakel bermangkuk isap.
statement.en: Marine biologist Bruce S. Wright was told by a local guide that limestone caves under a lake were home to the lusca, a large half-octopus, half-dragon animal with sucker-tipped tentacles.

claims.quote: Lusca is a clipped form of Mollusca (a phylum containing octopus, squid, cuttlefish, and other cephalopods), referring to the creature's varied mollusk features, such as tentacles.

statement.id: Nama Lusca adalah penggalan dari Mollusca, merujuk pada ciri moluska makhluk ini seperti tentakel.
statement.en: Lusca is a clipped form of Mollusca, referring to the creature's mollusc features such as tentacles.

short_description.id: Manipogo adalah monster danau dalam cerita rakyat Kanada yang konon hidup di Danau Manitoba, digambarkan sebagai makhluk mirip ular dengan punuk.
short_description.en: Manipogo is a lake monster of Canadian folklore said to live in Lake Manitoba, described as a serpent-like creature with a hump.

long_description.id: Manipogo adalah monster danau yang konon hidup di Danau Manitoba, Kanada. Namanya meniru Ogopogo dari British Columbia. Ia digambarkan bertubuh cokelat kehitaman dengan sedikitnya satu punuk di atas air; kepalanya disamakan dengan kepala kuda, unta, atau domba, atau disebut pipih berbentuk belah ketupat. Saat muncul ke permukaan, ia konon menjerit.
long_description.en: Manipogo is a lake monster said to live in Lake Manitoba, Canada. Its name echoes British Columbia's Ogopogo. It is described as brownish-black with at least one hump above the water; its head is likened to a horse's, camel's or sheep's, or said to be flat and diamond-shaped. It reportedly shrieks as it surfaces.

long_description.id: Penduduk First Nations setempat sudah lama punya legenda tentang makhluk mirip ular di danau itu. Penampakan pertama yang terdokumentasi oleh pemukim kulit putih dilaporkan pedagang bulu Valentine McKay pada September 1909. Pada 1936 nelayan Oscar Fredrickson konon menjaring sebuah tengkorak hewan, tetapi tengkorak itu hilang ketika rumahnya terbakar.
long_description.en: Local First Nations people have long told of serpent-like creatures in the lake. The first documented sighting by a white settler was reported by fur trader Valentine McKay in September 1909. In 1936 fisherman Oscar Fredrickson reportedly netted an animal skull, but it was lost when his house burned down.

long_description.id: Sebagian skeptis menduga yang terlihat sebenarnya rusa moose yang berenang. Makhluk ini memberi nama Taman Provinsi Manipogo, dan komunitas St. Laurent mengadakan Festival Manipogo setiap minggu pertama Maret.
long_description.en: Some sceptics think witnesses saw a swimming moose. The creature gives its name to Manipogo Provincial Park, and the community of St. Laurent holds a Manipogo Festival every first week of March.

role.id: Makhluk yang dilaporkan dalam penampakan sejak 1909.
role.en: A creature reported in sightings since 1909.

famous_for.en: The Manipogo Festival in St. Laurent.

did_you_know.id: Tengkorak yang diduga milik Manipogo konon hilang dalam kebakaran rumah.
did_you_know.en: A skull thought to be Manipogo's was reportedly lost in a house fire.

description.en: The lake where Manipogo is said to live.

short_description.id: Manticore adalah monster Persia pemakan manusia, bertubuh singa dan berwajah manusia.
short_description.en: The manticore is a Persian man-eating monster with a lion’s body and a human face.

long_description.id: Manticore adalah monster Persia pemakan manusia, bertubuh singa dan berwajah manusia. Nama manticore ditelusuri ke kata Persia untuk pemakan manusia.
long_description.en: The manticore is a Persian man-eating monster with a lion’s body and a human face. The name manticore is traced to a Persian word for man-eater.

long_description.id: Manticore juga muncul dalam bestiarium abad pertengahan. Uraian Ctesias yang dikutip memberi tiga baris gigi, telinga manusia, dan mata biru muda. Uraian itu menggambarkan ekor menyerupai kalajengking dengan sengat panjang. Pausanias menduga hewan dalam laporan Ctesias itu sebenarnya harimau. Manticore dipercaya tinggal di tempat sepi di luar permukiman.
long_description.en: The manticore also appears in medieval bestiaries. The quoted account of Ctesias gives it three rows of teeth, human ears, and light-blue eyes. That account depicts a scorpion-like tail with a long sting. Pausanias writes that he is inclined to think the reported creature is a tiger. The manticore is believed to inhabit lonely places outside communities.

short_description.id: Lyngbakr, "punggung semak heather", adalah monster laut raksasa mirip paus dalam Örvar-Odds saga yang menyamar sebagai pulau berlapis heather dan menenggelamkan pelaut yang mendarat di punggungnya.
short_description.en: Lyngbakr, 'heather-back', is a giant whale-like sea monster of the Örvar-Odds saga that poses as a heather-covered island and drowns sailors who land on its back.

long_description.id: Lyngbakr (bahasa Islandia lyngi, "heather", dan bak, "punggung") adalah nama monster laut raksasa mirip paus yang menurut Örvar-Odds saga hidup di Laut Greenland. Ia memancing pelaut dengan menyamar sebagai pulau yang ditumbuhi heather, dan ketika awak kapal mendarat di punggungnya, ia tenggelam ke laut sehingga mereka semua mati.
long_description.en: Lyngbakr (Icelandic lyngi, 'heather', and bak, 'back') is the name of a giant whale-like sea monster that, according to the Örvar-Odds saga, lived in the Greenland Sea. Pretending to be an island overgrown with heather, it tempted ships to put in; once sailors stepped onto its back it dived, and they all drowned.

long_description.id: Lyngbakur dianggap hewan laut terbesar dan sering terapung setengah tenggelam sehingga tampak seperti pulau yang ditumbuhi heather, dan banyak kisah tentangnya tersebar di Islandia. Dalam saga, awak Örvar-Oddr melewati dua batu yang muncul dari laut lalu sebuah pulau berlapis heather; menurut Vignir, "batu" dan "pulau" itu sebenarnya dua monster laut, Lyngbakr, paus terbesar di dunia, dan hafgufa.
long_description.en: The lyngbakur was thought the largest of all sea creatures, often lying half-submerged so it looked like a heather-grown island, and many tales of it circulate in Iceland. In the saga Örvar-Oddr's crew passed two rocks rising from the sea and then a large heather-covered island; Vignir told them these were in truth a pair of sea monsters, the hafgufa and Lyngbakr, mightiest of whales.

long_description.id: Sumber berbeda tentang nasib awak Oddr: satu uraian menyebut mereka berbalik dan pulau itu lenyap sebelum mereka mendarat, sedangkan kutipan teks saga menyebut lima orang Oddr naik ke pulau itu lalu tenggelam ketika pulau itu karam. Monster serupa dikenal dalam cerita rakyat Inuit Greenland sebagai Imap Umassoursa, dan dalam kisah Brendan sang pelaut sebagai paus Jasconius.
long_description.en: Sources differ on the fate of Oddr's men: one account says they turned back and the island vanished before they landed, whereas the quoted saga text says five of Oddr's men went onto the island and drowned when it sank. Similar monsters are known in Inuit lore of Greenland as Imap Umassoursa and in the tales of Brendan the Navigator as the whale Jasconius.

short_description.id: Tilberi atau snakkur adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Islandia yang diciptakan penyihir dari tulang rusuk manusia untuk mencuri susu ternak tetangga.
short_description.en: The tilberi or snakkur is a creature of Icelandic folklore, made by witches from a human rib to steal milk from the neighbours' livestock.

long_description.id: Tilberi ("pembawa") atau snakkur ("kumparan") adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Islandia yang dibuat penyihir untuk mencuri susu, dan hanya perempuan yang dapat membuat dan memilikinya. Kedua nama itu varian daerah; tidak ada catatan tertulis tentangnya sebelum abad ke-17, meski seorang penulis abad itu menyebut seorang penyihir dihukum karena memilikinya pada tahun 1500.
long_description.en: The tilberi ('carrier') or snakkur ('spindle') is an Icelandic folklore creature that witches made for stealing milk, and only women could create and keep one. The two names are regional variants; nothing was written about it before the 17th century, though one writer of that century mentions a witch punished in 1500 for owning one.

long_description.id: Untuk membuatnya, seorang perempuan mencuri tulang rusuk dari jenazah yang baru dikubur pada dini hari Minggu Pentakosta, membungkusnya dengan wol kelabu curian, dan menyimpannya di antara payudaranya. Pada tiga Minggu berikutnya ia meludahkan anggur komuni ke bungkusan itu hingga makin hidup, lalu membiarkannya menyusu di paha bagian dalam, yang meninggalkan benjolan mirip kutil.
long_description.en: To make one, a woman stole a rib from a freshly buried corpse early on Whitsunday, wrapped it in stolen grey wool and kept it between her breasts. Over the following three Sundays she spat communion wine onto the bundle, which grew livelier each time, then let it suck at her inner thigh, leaving a wart-like mark.

long_description.id: Tilberi lalu diutus menyedot susu sapi dan domba orang lain: ia melompat ke punggung hewan dan memanjangkan diri untuk mencapai ambing, lalu kembali ke jendela ruang susu pemiliknya dan memuntahkan susu curian ke tempat pengocok mentega. Mentega dari susu itu menggumpal atau mencair menjadi buih bila diberi tanda salib atau tanda sihir smjörhnútur.
long_description.en: The tilberi was then sent to drain other people's cows and ewes: it leapt on the animal's back and stretched down to the udder, then returned to its owner's dairy window and vomited the stolen milk into her churn. Butter from such milk curdled into clumps or dissolved into foam when a cross or the smjörhnútur sign was made over it.

long_description.id: Untuk menyingkirkannya, pemilik menyuruh tilberi mengumpulkan kotoran domba di padang penggembalaan; makhluk itu bekerja sampai mati atau mati karena tak tahan angka tiga, dan hanya tulang manusia yang tertinggal. Bila dikejar, ia lari bersembunyi di bawah rok "ibunya", sehingga perempuan dan makhluk itu dapat dibakar atau ditenggelamkan bersama.
long_description.en: To be rid of it, the owner ordered the tilberi to gather sheep droppings on the pasture; it worked itself to death or died because it could not endure the number three, leaving only the human bone behind. When chased it fled under its 'mother's' skirts, so that woman and creature could be burnt or drowned together.

famous_for.id: Mati karena tak tahan angka tiga.

did_you_know.id: Tilberi yang pulang membawa susu curian konon berseru "Perut penuh, Ibu!" di jendela ruang susu.
did_you_know.en: A tilberi returning with stolen milk was said to call out 'Full belly, Mummy!' at the dairy window.

statement.en: The tilberi or snakkur is an Icelandic folklore creature made by witches to steal milk; only women can make and own one.

statement.id: Tidak ada catatan tertulis sebelum abad ke-17, meski seorang penulis abad ke-17 menyebut penyihir yang dihukum karena memilikinya pada 1500.
statement.en: No written record exists before the 17th century, though a 17th-century writer mentions a witch punished in 1500 for owning one.

claims.quote: To create a tilberi, the woman steals a rib from a recently buried body early on Whitsunday, twists around it grey wool which she must steal for the purpose and keeps it between her breasts. ...  The next three Sundays at communion she spits the sanctified wine on the bundle, which will come more alive each time.

statement.id: Perempuan itu mencuri tulang rusuk jenazah yang baru dikubur pada dini hari Minggu Pentakosta, melilitnya dengan wol kelabu curian, dan menyimpannya di antara payudaranya.
statement.en: The woman steals a rib from a newly buried corpse early on Whitsunday, winds stolen grey wool round it and keeps it between her breasts.

claims.quote: It will return to the window of her dairy and call out "Full belly, Mummy!" or "Churn lid off, Mummy!" and vomit the stolen milk into her butter churn. To suck the milk from the animal's udder, it jumps on her back and lengthens itself to reach down

statement.id: Tilberi kembali ke jendela ruang susu, berseru "Perut penuh, Ibu!", dan memuntahkan susu curian ke pengocok mentega; untuk menyedot ambing ia melompat ke punggung hewan dan memanjangkan diri.
statement.en: It returns to the dairy window, calls 'Full belly, Mummy!' and vomits the stolen milk into the churn; to suck an udder it leaps onto the animal's back and stretches itself down.

claims.quote: Butter churned from milk stolen by a tilberi will clump together as if curdled, or even melt away into foam, if the sign of the cross is made over it or the smjörhnútur (butterknot) magical sign drawn in it.

statement.id: Mentega dari susu curian tilberi menggumpal atau mencair menjadi buih bila dibuat tanda salib di atasnya atau digambar tanda sihir smjörhnútur.
statement.en: Butter from milk a tilberi stole clumps or melts into foam if a cross is made over it or the smjörhnútur magic sign drawn in it.

claims.quote: The tilberi will then either work itself to death or die because as an evil creature it cannot tolerate the number three. Only the human bone will be left lying in the pasture.

statement.id: Tilberi akan bekerja sampai mati atau mati karena, sebagai makhluk jahat, tak tahan angka tiga; hanya tulang manusia yang tertinggal di padang.
statement.en: The tilberi either works itself to death or dies because, as an evil being, it cannot bear the number three; only the human bone remains in the pasture.

claims.quote: Un tilberi, ou Snakkur est une étrange créature du folklore de l'Islande. C'est une sorte de créature qui vole le lait du bétail des alentours et transforme le beurre fait à partir de ce lait en pièces d'or.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Prancis menyebut tilberi atau snakkur pencuri susu ternak sekitar yang mengubah mentega dari susu itu menjadi kepingan emas.
statement.en: The French article calls the tilberi or snakkur a thief of nearby livestock's milk that turns the butter made from it into gold coins.

claims.quote: Þegar hann kom, aðvaraði hann húsfreyju með þessum orðum: „Fullur beli, mamma“.

statement.id: Saat tiba, tilberi memberi tahu nyonya rumah dengan kata-kata "Fullur beli, mamma" ("Perut penuh, Ibu").
statement.en: When it arrived it warned the housewife with the words 'Fullur beli, mamma' ('Full belly, Mummy').

short_description.id: Marraco adalah naga atau momok penakut anak dari kota Lleida dalam mitos Katalan, bermulut cukup lebar untuk menelan manusia, kini diarak sebagai figur naga hijau dalam pesta kota.
short_description.en: The Marraco is a dragon or child-scaring bogey of Catalan myth in Lleida, with a mouth wide enough to swallow a person, now paraded as a green dragon figure at city festivals.

long_description.id: Lo Marraco adalah naga atau makhluk menakutkan dalam mitos Katalan di Lleida. Dalam cerita untuk menakuti anak, mulutnya cukup lebar untuk menelan manusia bulat-bulat; ia juga dikenal sebagai kadal sebesar naga yang memakan dot bayi sebagai lambang pertumbuhan. Nama marreco dipakai untuk momok serupa di Maestrat dan Menorca.
long_description.en: Lo Marraco is a dragon or fearsome creature of Catalan myth in Lleida. In tales to scare children its mouth could swallow a person whole; it is also known as a dragon-sized lizard that eats babies' dummies as a sign of growing up. The name marreco was used for a similar bogey in the Maestrat and Menorca.

long_description.id: Asal-usulnya diperdebatkan. Artikel bahasa Spanyol menyebutnya hewan totem dari abad ke-5 SM, tetapi artikel bahasa Katalan menyebut dugaan itu tidak berdasar karena totem kaum Ilerget adalah serigala. Figur naga dipakai dalam prosesi kota sejak 1551, dan menurut satu sumber properti tahun 1907-lah yang memberi makhluk ini bentuk dan warna. Figur sekarang, naga hijau tanpa sayap sepanjang 8,5 m yang mengeluarkan asap dari hidung, dibuat pada 1957.
long_description.en: Its origin is disputed. The Spanish article calls it a totem animal from the 5th century BC, but the Catalan article calls this baseless, since the Ilergetes' totem was the wolf. A dragon figure joined city processions from 1551, and one authority says the 1907 prop gave the creature its shape and colour. The present figure, a wingless green dragon 8.5 m long that blows smoke from its nostrils, was built in 1957.

famous_for.id: Figur naga hijau dalam pesta Lleida.
famous_for.en: The green dragon figure of Lleida's festivals.

did_you_know.id: Kata Katalan marraco juga berarti sejenis hiu.
did_you_know.en: The Catalan word marraco also means a kind of shark.

claims.quote: The Marraco (Catalan: Lo Marraco, Catalan pronunciation: [məˈraku])  is a dragon or frightening creature in Catalan myth in the city of Lleida. It possessed a mouth wide enough to swallow a human whole according to tales told to frighten children.

statement.id: Marraco (bahasa Katalan: Lo Marraco) adalah naga atau makhluk menakutkan dalam mitos Katalan di kota Lleida; menurut cerita untuk menakuti anak, mulutnya cukup lebar untuk menelan manusia bulat-bulat.
statement.en: The Marraco (Catalan: Lo Marraco) is a dragon or frightening creature of Catalan myth in the city of Lleida; in tales told to frighten children, its mouth was wide enough to swallow a person whole.

claims.quote: Amb el nom de lo Marraco es coneix a la ciutat de Lleida un lluert de la mida d'un drac, amb una boca especialment ampla i grossa amb la qual es menja els xumets dels infants, com a símbol del seu creixement.

statement.id: Di Lleida, Lo Marraco dikenal sebagai kadal sebesar naga dengan mulut sangat lebar yang memakan dot bayi, sebagai lambang pertumbuhan anak.
statement.en: In Lleida, Lo Marraco is known as a dragon-sized lizard with a very wide mouth that eats babies' dummies, as a symbol of their growing up.

claims.quote: Lo Marraco és també un espantamainades tradicional de Lleida. Hi ha altres indrets on es feia servir el mateix nom (en la variant, però, marreco) per a fer por a la mainada, com ara el Maestrat i Menorca.

statement.id: Lo Marraco juga momok penakut anak tradisional Lleida; nama yang sama (dalam varian marreco) dipakai untuk menakuti anak di tempat lain seperti Maestrat dan Menorca.
statement.en: Lo Marraco is also a traditional child-scarer of Lleida; the same name (as marreco) was used to frighten children elsewhere, such as the Maestrat and Menorca.

claims.quote: El Marraco es un animal totémico de Lérida que data del siglo V a. C. Como animal mitológico no ha existido nunca y su representación es libre.

statement.id: Menurut artikel bahasa Spanyol, Marraco adalah hewan totem Lérida dari abad ke-5 SM yang wujudnya bebas digambarkan.
statement.en: According to the Spanish article, the Marraco is a totem animal of Lérida dating from the 5th century BC, freely represented.

claims.quote: La veritat, però, és que tant aquestes conjectures com el fet d'atribuir al basc l'origen del nom (sovint es diu que "marraco" vol dir 'drac' en aquesta llengua) no tenen cap fonament històric ni científic. D'altra banda, l'animal totèmic dels ilergets era el llop, no pas el drac.

statement.id: Artikel bahasa Katalan menegaskan bahwa dugaan asal-usul kuno itu, juga anggapan namanya berasal dari kata Basque untuk naga, tidak berdasar sejarah maupun ilmiah; hewan totem kaum Ilerget adalah serigala, bukan naga.
statement.en: The Catalan article stresses that these ancient-origin conjectures, and the idea that the name comes from Basque for 'dragon', have no historical or scientific basis; the totem animal of the Ilergetes was the wolf, not the dragon.

claims.quote: However, this is contradicted by a different authority, which notes that it was the advent of the marraco prop built in 1907 for the parade which "gave shape and color to this imaginary creature".

statement.en: Another authority notes that the marraco prop built in 1907 for the parade 'gave shape and color to this imaginary creature'.

statement.id: Salah satu pendahulu Lo Marraco de Lleida yang tercatat adalah figur naga yang dipakai kota itu dalam prosesi Maria Diangkat ke Surga tahun 1551.

statement.en: The figure is 8.5 m long, 2.90 m wide and 3.75 m high and weighs over two tonnes; it is a wingless green dragon with very sharp fangs that blows smoke from its nose.

short_description.id: Meduza atau Meluza adalah makhluk mitis dalam cerita rakyat Rusia, digambarkan pada lubok abad ke-17 atau ke-18 sebagai setengah perempuan setengah ular atau ikan.
short_description.en: Meduza or Meluza is a mythical creature of Russian folklore, shown in a 17th- or 18th-century lubok as half woman and half snake or fish.

long_description.id: Meduza, juga disebut Meluza ("yang kecil") atau Meluzina, adalah makhluk mitis dalam cerita rakyat Rusia yang digambarkan pada lubok (gambar cetak rakyat) abad ke-17 atau ke-18. Ia dilukiskan sebagai setengah perempuan setengah ular, atau setengah perempuan setengah ikan, dan juga disebut dewi tipu daya.
long_description.en: Meduza, also called Meluza ("little one") or Meluzina, is a mythical creature of Russian folklore depicted in a lubok (popular print) of the 17th or 18th century. She is shown as half woman and half snake, or half woman and half fish, and is also said to be a deity of deception.

long_description.id: Ia digambarkan sebagai monster laut berkepala gadis cantik berambut gelap dan bermahkota, bertubuh binatang belang, berekor naga yang ujungnya mulut ular, dan berkaki seperti gajah yang ujungnya juga mulut ular. Mulut-mulut ular itu dipercaya mengandung racun naga yang mematikan. Ia tinggal di laut dekat jurang Ethiopia atau di Samudra Barat.
long_description.en: The lubok shows a sea creature whose crowned head is that of a lovely dark-haired girl, set on a striped animal's body, with a dragon's tail ending in a snake's mouth, and elephant-like legs that also end in snake mouths. Those snake mouths were believed to hold deadly dragon venom. Her home was said to be either the Western Ocean or the waters by the Ethiopian abyss.

long_description.id: Ia juga disebut dalam "Kitab Ilmu Alam" yang dikaitkan dengan Nikolai Spathari. Menurut B. M. Sokolov, kisah pada lubok ini misterius tetapi merujuk pada tema yang dikenal dari tradisi lisan.
long_description.en: She is also mentioned in the "Book of Natural Science" attributed to Nikolai Spathari. According to B. M. Sokolov, the subject of this lubok is mysterious but refers to a theme known from oral narrative.

short_description.id: Drak adalah roh rumah tangga terbang dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, berwujud naga kecil berekor menyala, yang membawakan gandum, mentega, dan emas curian ke pemiliknya.
short_description.en: The Drak is a flying household spirit of German folklore, shaped like a small dragon with a glowing tail, which brings stolen grain, butter and gold to its owner.

long_description.id: Drak, yang juga disebut Fürdrak atau Drakel, adalah roh rumah tangga dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang sering disamakan dengan kobold atau iblis. Meski kadang dinamai Drache (naga) dan tampak seperti naga, ia hampir tak berhubungan dengan naga reptil. Namanya diduga bukan turunan langsung dari kata Latin draco, melainkan dari mandragora.
long_description.en: The Drak, also called Fürdrak or Drakel, is a household spirit of German folklore often equated with the kobold or the devil. Although sometimes named Drache (dragon) and dragon-like in looks, it has little to do with the reptilian dragon. Its name is thought to come not directly from Latin draco but from mandragora.

long_description.id: Drak dikenal di Jerman utara dan tengah serta wilayah Slavia di sekitarnya. Ia terbang lewat cerobong untuk membawa gandum, mentega, daging asap, ham, dan emas kepada petani, sehingga banyak petani kaya diisukan memelihara Drak. Wujudnya naga kecil berekor menyala, tetapi di Pomerania timur ia juga digambarkan sebagai ular api berkepala bebek atau kuali menyala berekor; ia bisa pula menjadi angsa kelabu atau ayam basah.
long_description.en: The Drak is known in northern and central Germany and nearby Slavic lands. It flies down the chimney with grain, butter, bacon, ham and gold for the farmer, so many prosperous farmers were rumoured to keep one. It looks like a small dragon with a glowing tail, but in eastern Pomerania it is also pictured as a fiery snake with a duck's head or a glowing kettle with a tail; it can also become a grey goose or a wet hen.

long_description.id: Kepemilikan Drak sering dikaitkan dengan perjanjian dengan iblis. Ia tinggal di perapian atau jauh di dalam tungku, harus diberi makan kue, daging, susu, atau bubur jawawut, dan bila tidak diberi makan ia membalas dendam, biasanya dengan menyulut kebakaran. Orang yang melihatnya terbang dapat memaksanya menjatuhkan sebagian harta dengan seruan seperti "lat fallen, wat nich dien hört" ("jatuhkan yang bukan milikmu").
long_description.en: Owning a Drak was often tied to a pact with the devil. It lives in the hearth or deep in the oven, must be fed with cakes, meat, milk or millet porridge, and if left unfed it takes revenge, typically by starting a fire. Anyone who sees it flying can force it to drop part of its treasure with a formula such as 'lat fallen, wat nich dien hört' ('drop what isn't yours').

statement.en: The Drak (also Fürdrak, Drakel) is a household spirit of German folklore often equated with the Kobold or devil (Teufel); it is also called Drache (dragon) but has little to do with the reptile monster.

claims.quote: Der Drak (oder auch Fürdrak, Drakel, Alf, Stöpke und Gluswanz genannt) ist ein fliegender Hausgeist. Obwohl er äußerlich einem Drachen ähnelt, hat er mit diesem wohl nichts gemeinsam.

statement.id: Drak (juga disebut Fürdrak, Drakel, Alf, Stöpke, dan Gluswanz) adalah roh rumah terbang; meski tampak seperti naga, ia agaknya tak ada kaitannya dengan naga.
statement.en: The Drak (also called Fürdrak, Drakel, Alf, Stöpke and Gluswanz) is a flying house spirit; though it looks like a dragon it probably has nothing in common with one.

claims.quote: Er ist in Nord- und Mitteldeutschland beheimatet, sowie auch in angrenzenden slawischen Gebieten und bringt dem Bauern durch den Kamin Korn, Getreide, Butter, Speck, Schinken und Gold. Daher wurde vielen wohlhabenden Bauern auch nachgesagt, dass sie einen Drak in ihren Diensten hätten.

statement.id: Drak berasal dari Jerman utara dan tengah (Nord- und Mitteldeutschland) serta wilayah Slavia di sekitarnya, dan membawa gandum, mentega, daging asap, ham, dan emas kepada petani lewat cerobong; karena itu banyak petani kaya diisukan memelihara Drak.
statement.en: The Drak is at home in northern and central Germany (Nord- und Mitteldeutschland) and adjacent Slavic areas and brings the farmer corn, grain, butter, bacon, ham and gold through the chimney; hence many wealthy farmers were said to have a Drak in service.

statement.en: The Drak looks like a small dragon with a glowing tail as it travels through the air; in eastern Pomerania (Pommern) it is called Alf, and in places a fiery snake with a duck's head or a glowing kettle with a tail.

statement.id: Drac terbang di udara dan masuk rumah lewat cerobong atau lubang atap; ia berwujud batang menyala, lelaki kecil berompi merah, atau hewan seperti ayam dan kadal, kadang bola api; ia erat dengan api dan tinggal di perapian atau jauh di dalam tungku.
statement.en: Drac flies through the air and enters by the chimney or a hole in the roof; it takes the form of a burning pole, a little man in a red vest, or an animal such as a hen or lizard, at times a fireball; it is closely bound to fire and lives in the hearth or deep in the oven.

Draca bylo nutno živit, podávaly se mu tak pokrmy jako koláče, maso, mléko nebo jáhlová kaše. Když není krmen, tak se mstí, typicky založením požáru.

short_description.id: Putri Duyung Warsawa (Syrenka) adalah lambang kota Warsawa yang tampil pada lambang kota dan banyak patung, dikisahkan siap melindungi kota dengan pedang dan perisai.
short_description.en: The Mermaid of Warsaw (Syrenka) is the symbol of Warsaw, shown on its coat of arms and many statues, and said to stand ready to defend the city with sword and shield.

long_description.id: Putri Duyung Warsawa adalah lambang kota Warsawa dan tampil pada lambang kota serta pada banyak patung dan gambar lain. Kata Polandia syrenka seakar dengan "siren", tetapi sosok ini lebih tepat disebut melusina, putri duyung air tawar. Melusina sendiri adalah roh air tawar bersayap dan berekor ikan yang hidup di sungai atau sumur.
long_description.en: The Mermaid of Warsaw is the symbol of the city of Warsaw, appearing on its coat of arms and in many statues and other images. The Polish word syrenka is related to "siren", but the figure is more properly a freshwater mermaid called a melusina. A melusina is a winged, fish-tailed freshwater spirit living in rivers or wells.

long_description.id: Wujudnya pada lambang kota berubah dari masa ke masa. Pada 1390 lambang Warsawa memuat makhluk berkaki burung dengan tubuh bersisik naga; segel tahun 1459 menampilkan ciri perempuan, tubuh burung, tangan manusia, ekor ikan, serta kaki dan cakar burung; dan wujud putri duyung pertama berasal dari 1622 dan bertahan sampai sekarang. Ia memegang perisai di tangan kiri dan pedang di tangan kanan. Ilham lambang ini kemungkinan berasal dari buku Physiologus abad ke-2.
long_description.en: Its form on the coat of arms changed over time. In 1390 the Warsaw arms showed a creature with bird legs and a dragon-scaled body; the seal of 1459 had female features, a bird body, human hands, a fish tail and bird legs and claws; and the first mermaid form dates from 1622 and remains in use. She holds a shield in her left hand and a sword in her right. The arms were probably inspired by the 2nd-century book Physiologus.

long_description.id: Ada beberapa legenda tentangnya. Menurut kisah yang dituturkan pemandu wisata, putri duyung itu singgah di tepi sungai dekat Kota Tua dan memutuskan menetap; para nelayan yang kesal karena jaring mereka kusut dan ikan-ikan dilepaskan hendak menangkapnya, tetapi jatuh cinta setelah mendengar nyanyiannya. Ketika seorang saudagar kaya menangkap dan mengurungnya, para nelayan membebaskannya, dan sejak itu ia siap melindungi kota dengan pedang dan perisai. Versi lain menyebut ia menolong seorang pangeran yang tersesat saat berburu, lalu pangeran itu mendirikan kota untuk menghormatinya.
long_description.en: There are several legends about her. In the tale told by city guides, the mermaid paused on a riverbank near the Old Town and chose to stay; fishermen annoyed by tangled nets and freed fish planned to trap her but fell in love on hearing her sing. When a rich merchant caught and caged her, the fishermen set her free, and ever since she has stood ready to guard the city with sword and shield. Another version says she helped a prince lost while hunting, and he founded the city in her honour.

long_description.id: Kadang legenda ini diperluas dengan menyebut Putri Duyung Kecil di Kopenhagen sebagai saudarinya, yang berpisah jalan dengannya dari Laut Baltik. Di Warsawa terdapat banyak patungnya, antara lain karya Konstanty Hegel di alun-alun Kota Tua dan patung karya Ludwika Nitschowa yang didirikan pada April 1939 di Powiśle dekat Sungai Vistula.
long_description.en: The legend is sometimes extended to make the Little Mermaid of Copenhagen her sister, the two parting ways from the Baltic Sea. Warsaw has many statues of her, among them Konstanty Hegel's in the Old Town Square and Ludwika Nitschowa's, set up in April 1939 in Powiśle by the Vistula river.

short_description.id: Feldgeister ("roh ladang") atau Korndämonen ("setan gandum") adalah roh-roh pertanian dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang menghuni ladang gandum, berwujud hewan atau manusia.
short_description.en: Feldgeister ('field spirits') or Korndämonen ('corn demons') are agricultural spirits of German folklore who inhabit the grain fields in animal or human form.

long_description.id: Feldgeister atau Korndämonen adalah roh gandum dalam cerita rakyat Jerman, dan sering juga roh angin yang mendatangkan kilat dan hujan. Istilah Korndämonen diperkenalkan Wilhelm Mannhardt sebagai sebutan kolektif bagi makhluk gaib di ladang gandum atau tanaman lain seperti rami, kacang, dan opium; menurut artikel bahasa Jerman, sebutan "Korngeist" sebenarnya lebih tepat.
long_description.en: Feldgeister or Korndämonen are corn spirits of German folklore, and often also wind spirits that bring lightning and rain. The term Korndämonen was coined by Wilhelm Mannhardt as a collective name for supernatural beings in grain fields or other crops such as flax, beans and poppies; the German article notes that 'Korngeist' would really be the better label.

long_description.id: Feldgeister dikenal dalam banyak bentuk, ada yang berwujud hewan seperti serigala gandum (Roggenwolf), anjing, kucing, babi, kambing, dan ayam jantan, ada pula yang berwujud manusia seperti Roggenmuhme, Hafermann, dan Kornkind. Banyak di antaranya ditakuti karena mencuri atau menyakiti anak-anak; kehadiran setan gandum terlihat pada gandum yang bergelombang, seperti dalam ungkapan "Ibu Gandum ada di ladang".
long_description.en: Feldgeister come in many shapes: animal forms such as the rye wolf (Roggenwolf), dogs, cats, pigs, goats and roosters, and human forms such as the Roggenmuhme, the Hafermann and the Kornkind. Many are feared for stealing or harming children; a corn demon's presence is seen in the waving of the grain, as in the saying 'the Corn Mother is in the field'.

long_description.id: Saat panen, roh-roh itu lari makin dalam ke ladang menghindari para penyabit dan akhirnya terperangkap di batang gandum terakhir. Ia lalu dibunuh dengan dipotong atau diirik, atau dibawa ke desa dengan upacara dalam wujud boneka gandum; bulir terakhir dan buah pohon sering ditinggalkan sebagai persembahan. Sentuhan langsung dengan roh ladang menyebabkan sakit.
long_description.en: At harvest the spirits flee deeper into the field away from the mowers and are finally trapped in the last stalks. The spirit is then killed by cutting or threshing, or carried ceremonially to the village as a corn doll; the last ears and tree fruits are often left as an offering. Direct contact with a field spirit brings illness.

long_description.id: Korndämonen dianggap berasal dari dewa-dewa tumbuhan bangsa petani yang dahulu dipuja untuk melindungi tanaman. Seiring waktu makna aslinya hilang dan mereka didemonisasi, menjadi sosok menakutkan yang mencegah anak-anak memasuki dan merusak ladang yang sedang matang. Konsep roh gandum dipopulerkan pada awal abad ke-20 oleh antropolog Inggris James Frazer.
long_description.en: Korndämonen are thought to stem from the vegetation gods of farming peoples, once worshipped to protect the crops. Over time their original meaning faded and they were demonised into bogeys that kept children from entering and trampling the ripening fields. The idea of the corn spirit was popularised in the early 20th century by the British anthropologist James Frazer.

role.en: Trapped in the last stalks of grain.

famous_for.id: Menakut-nakuti anak agar tak masuk ladang.
famous_for.en: Scares children away from the fields.

did_you_know.id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat, roh ladang terperangkap di batang gandum terakhir yang dipanen, lalu dibawa ke desa dalam wujud boneka gandum.
did_you_know.en: Folk belief held that the field spirit was trapped in the last stalks harvested and carried to the village as a corn doll.

claims.quote: During harvest season Feldgeister flee deeper into the fields to escape the mowers. With the last cornstalks the corn spirit becomes trapped. statement.id: Feldgeister (Feldgeist, Korndämonen) adalah roh gandum dalam cerita rakyat Jerman yang sering juga roh angin; saat panen mereka lari makin dalam ke ladang, terperangkap di batang terakhir, lalu dibunuh dengan dipotong atau diirik, atau dibawa ke desa dengan upacara sebagai boneka gandum; sentuhan langsung menyebabkan sakit.
statement.en: Feldgeister (Feldgeist, Korndämonen) are corn spirits of German folklore, often also wind spirits; at harvest they flee deeper into the field, are trapped in the last stalks, then killed by cutting or threshing, or brought ceremonially to the village as a corn doll; direct contact causes illness.

claims.quote: Numerous Feldgeister are known in German folklore, some shaped as animals, some in human form. The last grain heads and tree fruits are often left at their place as a sacrifice for the agricultural spirits.

statement.en: Many Feldgeister are known in German folklore, some animal-shaped, some human; the last ears of grain and tree fruits are often left in place as an offering.

claims.quote: The Roggenwolf ("rye wolf"), Getreidewolf ("grain wolf") or Kornwolf ("corn wolf") is a field spirit shaped as a wolf. The Roggenwolf steals children and feeds on them.

statement.en: The Roggenwolf ('rye wolf') is a wolf-shaped field spirit that steals and eats children; other examples include the human-shaped Roggenmuhme, Hafermann and Kornkind.

claims.quote: Ihren Ursprung haben Korndämonen in früheren Vegetationsgöttern agrarisch orientierter Völker. Diese Götter wurden angebetet, damit sie die Feldfrüchte schützen und fördern. Im Lauf der Zeit verschwand jedoch die ursprüngliche Bedeutung dieser Götter und sie wurden dämonisiert. Sie dienten nun als Schreckgestalt dazu, Kinder vom Betreten und damit Zerstören der reifenden Felder abzuhalten.

statement.id: Korndämonen berasal dari dewa tumbuhan bangsa petani yang dipuja agar melindungi tanaman; seiring waktu makna asli itu hilang, mereka didemonisasi, dan menjadi sosok menakutkan yang mencegah anak-anak memasuki dan merusak ladang yang matang.
statement.en: Korndämonen originate in the vegetation gods of farming peoples, worshipped to protect crops; over time that meaning faded, they were demonised and became bogeys keeping children out of ripening fields.

claims.quote: Polní duch je druh mytické bytosti, která přebývá v obilném poli a střeží ho. statement.id: Roh ladang (polní duch) adalah makhluk mitis yang menghuni dan menjaga ladang gandum; istilah dan konsepnya muncul dalam karya folklorist Jerman Wilhelm Mannhardt pada 1860-an dan dipopulerkan antropolog Inggris (British) James Frazer pada awal abad ke-20.
statement.en: The field spirit (polní duch) is a mythical being that lives in and guards the grain field; the term and idea first appeared in the 1860s work of German folklorist Wilhelm Mannhardt and were popularised by British anthropologist James Frazer in the early 20th century.

statement.id: Etnografer Drahomíra Stránská mengakui sumbangan Mannhardt tetapi berpendapat kebiasaan tersebut berakar pada aspek praktis kehidupan pertanian, bukan agama.
statement.en: Ethnographer Drahomíra Stránská acknowledged Mannhardt's contribution but held that the customs arose from practical sides of farm life rather than from religion.

short_description.id: Michigan Dogman adalah makhluk mirip anjing berkaki dua dalam legenda modern Michigan, yang menurut catatan berawal dari lagu lelucon April Mop Steve Cook tahun 1987.
short_description.en: The Michigan Dogman is a two-legged dog-like creature of modern Michigan legend which, by the record, began with Steve Cook's 1987 April Fool's song.

long_description.id: Michigan Dogman digambarkan sebagai anjing berkaki dua setinggi 2,1 m bertubuh manusia dengan lolongan seperti jeritan manusia, yang konon pertama terlihat pada 1887 di Wexford County dan muncul setiap tahun berakhiran tujuh. Namun catatan yang terdokumentasi berawal pada 1987, ketika Steve Cook memutar lagu The Legend sebagai lelucon April Mop; Cook mengaku mengarangnya sendiri, dan klaim legenda Odawa tidak pernah punya sumber autentik.
long_description.en: The Michigan Dogman is described as a 2.1 m two-legged canine with a man's torso and a scream-like howl, said to have been first seen in 1887 in Wexford County and to return in years ending in seven. But the documented record begins in 1987, when Steve Cook played his song The Legend as an April Fool's joke; Cook said he invented it, and the claimed Odawa legend has no authentic source.

long_description.id: Setelah lagu itu, banyak pendengar mengaku bertemu makhluk serupa. Kriptozoologi menggolongkannya makhluk mirip anjing yang berjalan tegak, sedangkan folkloris menganggapnya legenda regional modern.
long_description.en: After the song, many listeners claimed to have met such a creature. Cryptozoology classes it as an upright canid, while folklorists treat it as a modern regional legend.

who.en: A two-legged canine with a man's torso.

description.id: Lagu lelucon April Mop yang melahirkan legenda ini.
description.en: The April Fool's song that launched the legend.

claims.quote: In folklore, the Michigan Dogman is an alleged creature first witnessed in 1887 in Wexford County, Michigan, United States. It was described as a seven-foot-tall (2.1 m), blue- or amber-eyed bipedal canid possessing the torso of a man with a fearsome howl resembling a human scream.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat, Michigan Dogman adalah makhluk yang konon pertama terlihat pada 1887 di Wexford County, Michigan, Amerika Serikat, digambarkan sebagai anjing berkaki dua setinggi tujuh kaki (2,1 m) bermata biru atau kuning, bertubuh manusia, dengan lolongan seperti jeritan manusia.
statement.en: In folklore the Michigan Dogman is an alleged creature first seen in 1887 in Wexford County, Michigan, United States, described as a seven-foot (2.1 m), blue- or amber-eyed two-legged canine with a man's torso and a howl like a human scream.

claims.quote: Folklore claims that the creature reemerges on a recurring ten-year pattern linked to years ending in the number seven.

statement.id: Menurut cerita rakyat, makhluk ini muncul kembali setiap sepuluh tahun pada tahun yang berakhiran angka tujuh.
statement.en: Folklore says the creature reappears every ten years, in years ending in seven.

claims.quote: In 1987, disc jockey Steve Cook at WTCM-FM in Traverse City, Michigan, recorded a song titled "The Legend", which he initially played as an April Fool's Day joke.

statement.id: Pada 1987 penyiar radio Steve Cook di WTCM-FM, Traverse City, merekam lagu The Legend yang mula-mula diputar sebagai lelucon April Mop.
statement.en: In 1987 disc jockey Steve Cook of WTCM-FM in Traverse City recorded a song, The Legend, first played as an April Fool's joke.

claims.quote: I made it up completely from my own imagination as an April Fools' prank for the radio and stumbled my way to a legend that goes back all the way to Native American times.

statement.id: Cook mengaku mengarang lagu itu sepenuhnya dari imajinasinya sebagai lelucon April Mop untuk radio.
statement.en: Cook said he made it up entirely from his own imagination as an April Fools' prank for the radio.

claims.quote: After he played the song, Cook received calls from listeners who said that they had encountered a similar creature.

statement.id: Setelah lagu itu diputar, Cook menerima telepon dari pendengar yang mengaku pernah bertemu makhluk serupa.
statement.en: After he played the song, Cook got calls from listeners who said they had met a similar creature.

short_description.id: Minhocão adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Brasil, digambarkan sebagai cacing atau ikan raksasa yang menyeret ternak ke dalam air dan meninggalkan parit dalam.
short_description.en: The Minhocão is a creature of Brazilian folklore, described as a giant worm or fish that drags livestock under water and leaves deep trenches.

long_description.id: Minhocão adalah makhluk cerita rakyat Brasil yang diklaim berupa ikan besar atau menyerupai cacing raksasa; namanya bentuk pembesar dari minhoca, "cacing tanah" dalam bahasa Portugis. Ia konon mencabut pohon, meninggalkan parit dalam, dan menyukai tempat lembap.
long_description.en: The Minhocão is a creature of Brazilian folklore said to be a large fish or a giant worm; its name is an augmentative of minhoca, Portuguese for "earthworm". It was said to uproot trees, leave deep trenches and prefer damp places.

long_description.id: Penduduk setempat menceritakannya kepada naturalis Eropa pada abad ke-19. Pada Desember 1846 Augustin Saint-Hilaire mencatat Minhocão di danau Padre Aranda dan Feia yang konon menyeret kuda dan sapi ke dalam air, dan menduganya sejenis ikan paru besar. Fritz Müller melaporkannya dalam jurnal Jerman pada 1878, dan kriptozoolog Karl Shuker kemudian mengaitkannya dengan Sachamama dari Peru.
long_description.en: Locals described it to European naturalists in the 19th century. In December 1846 Augustin Saint-Hilaire recorded Minhocão in the Padre Aranda and Feia lakes that dragged horses and cattle under water, and guessed it was a large lungfish. Fritz Müller reported it in a German journal in 1878, and cryptozoologist Karl Shuker later linked it with the Sachamama of Peru.

who.id: Cacing atau ikan raksasa dari Brasil.

short_description.id: Monster Ravenna adalah kelahiran aneh yang dilaporkan di Ravenna pada 1512, bertanduk dan bersayap kelelawar, yang ditafsirkan sebagai pertanda Pertempuran Ravenna.
short_description.en: The Monster of Ravenna is a monstrous birth reported at Ravenna in 1512, horned and bat-winged, read as an omen of the Battle of Ravenna.

long_description.id: Monster Ravenna adalah kelahiran aneh yang dilaporkan di dekat Ravenna pada awal 1512, mungkin apokrif. Catatan harian Tedallini menyebutnya anak biarawati dan biarawan yang bertanduk, bertanda YXV di dada, dan berkaki aneh; Luca Landucci menambahkan sayap kelelawar, mata di lutut, dan kaki bercakar elang. Bayi itu ditelantarkan hingga mati atas perintah Paus.
long_description.en: The Monster of Ravenna is a monstrous birth reported near Ravenna in early 1512, possibly apocryphal. Tedallini's diary calls it the child of a nun and a friar, horned, marked YXV on the chest and with strange legs; Luca Landucci added bat wings, an eye on the knee and an eagle's clawed foot. The infant was left to die on the Pope's order.

long_description.id: Ia paling sering ditafsirkan sebagai pertanda Pertempuran Ravenna (1512), dan tanda di dadanya dibaca sebagai pesan moral; tahun kelahirannya pun berbeda antara Lycosthenes (1511) dan Boaistuau (1512). Pihak Katolik maupun Protestan memakainya sebagai simbol. Konsensus medis modern menganggapnya anak dengan kelainan bawaan berat.
long_description.en: It was most often read as an omen of the Battle of Ravenna (1512), and the signs on its chest as a moral message; even its birth year differs between Lycosthenes (1511) and Boaistuau (1512). Catholic and Protestant opponents both used it as a symbol. Modern medical consensus sees a child with a severe congenital disorder.

statement.en: The Monster of Ravenna was a possibly apocryphal monstrous birth of the late Renaissance whose appearance near Ravenna in early 1512 was widely reported in European pamphlets and diaries of the time.

claims.quote: Images of its grotesque features were interpreted symbolically by opponents of both the Catholic Church and the Protestant Reformation, although a more common explanation at the time was that the beast was an omen regarding the outcome of the Battle of Ravenna (1512).

statement.id: Gambaran rupanya yang aneh ditafsirkan secara simbolis oleh penentang Gereja Katolik maupun Reformasi Protestan, tetapi penjelasan yang lebih umum saat itu ialah bahwa makhluk itu pertanda hasil Pertempuran Ravenna (1512).
statement.en: Its grotesque features were read symbolically by opponents of both the Catholic Church and the Protestant Reformation, though the commoner explanation then was that it was an omen of the Battle of Ravenna (1512).

claims.quote: Modern medical consensus identifies the monster as a child with some variety of severe congenital disorder.
